03: Feature Engineering¶

Objective¶

Create temporal, lag, and external features for time series forecasting models based on EDA findings from 02_eda.ipynb.

Tasks¶

  • Load weekly bed occupancy data from 01b_data_preprocessing.ipynb
  • Perform train/test split (chronological, preserving temporal order)
  • Create temporal features (week of year, month, quarter, holidays)
  • Generate lag features based on ACF/PACF analysis (lags 1, 3, 4, 52)
  • Create rolling statistics (4-week, 13-week, 52-week windows)
  • Add external features based on EDA correlation analysis
  • Apply differencing for stationarity (as indicated by ADF/KPSS tests)
  • NEW: Include ICU and COVID KPIs for VAR model

Data Source: COVID-19 Hospital Capacity dataset for ADVENTHEALTH ORLANDO Date Range: 2020-07-19 to 2024-04-21 (197 weeks)

EDA-Driven Feature Selection¶

Based on 02_eda.ipynb findings:

Strong Predictors (include in models):

  • ili - ILI rate (r = 0.387, p < 0.0001) - strongest flu predictor
  • temp_min - Minimum temperature (r = -0.254, p = 0.0003) - strongest weather predictor

Exclude (redundant or not significant):

  • flu_activity_level, wili - Redundant with ili (r ≈ 1.0 correlation)
  • temp_avg, temp_max - Redundant with temp_min (r > 0.95)
  • precipitation, wind_speed, pressure - Not statistically significant
  • is_flu_season - Not statistically significant (p = 0.20)

Time Series Characteristics:

  • Non-stationary (ADF p=0.21, KPSS p=0.01) → Differencing needed
  • Strong autocorrelation at lag 1 (r = 0.898)
  • PACF significant at lags 1, 3, 4, 10, 14
  • 52-week seasonality (moderate strength: 0.375)
  • Increasing trend: 23% increase from 2020 to 2024

VAR Model KPIs (Granger Causality Results)¶

Based on 02_eda.ipynb Granger causality tests:

Include in VAR (Granger-causes bed_occupancy):

  • covid_patient_pct ✅ Significant at lags 2, 3, 5, 8 (p < 0.05)
    • Cross-correlation shows it LEADS bed_occupancy by 14 weeks (predictive!)
    • 76.6% complete (missing early 2020 data)

Exclude from VAR (does NOT Granger-cause bed_occupancy):

  • icu_occupancy_rate ❌ Not significant at any lag tested (1-8)
    • May still be useful for other purposes but doesn't improve bed_occupancy forecasts

VAR Configuration:

  • Endogenous: ['bed_occupancy', 'covid_patient_pct']
  • Lag order: 8 weeks (based on Granger significance)
  • Apply differencing to non-stationary series

CENTRALIZED FEATURE CONFIGURATION¶

ALL model-specific feature definitions are defined here. Model notebooks (04a-04e) should load these configurations rather than defining their own.

This ensures consistency across all models and makes it easy to update feature selections.

In [ ]:
# ============================================================================
# CENTRALIZED FEATURE CONFIGURATION (Single Source of Truth)
# ============================================================================
# All model-specific feature definitions are defined here.
# Model notebooks (04b, 04c, 04d, 04e) load from feature_config.json
# ============================================================================

print("="*70)
print("📋 CENTRALIZED FEATURE CONFIGURATION")
print("="*70)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# UNIVERSAL FEATURE DEFINITIONS (Based on 02_eda.ipynb analysis)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# CRITICAL features - must include in all models if available
# These have the strongest predictive power based on EDA
# FIXED: Use LAGGED external features to avoid data leakage
CRITICAL_FEATURES = [
    'bed_occupancy_lag_1',      # Strongest autocorrelation (r=0.898)
    'rolling_mean_4',           # Short-term trend (r=0.846)
    'bed_occupancy_lag_52',     # Annual seasonality
    'ili_lag_1',                # Strong external predictor (lagged to avoid leakage)
]

# HIGH priority features - include if feature budget allows
# FIXED: Use LAGGED versions to avoid data leakage
HIGH_PRIORITY_FEATURES = [
    'bed_occupancy_lag_4',      # Monthly pattern
    'bed_occupancy_lag_3',      # Short-term momentum
    'rolling_mean_52',          # Long-term trend
    'rolling_std_4',            # Short-term volatility
    'temp_min_lag_1',           # Weather predictor (lagged to avoid leakage)
    'covid_patient_pct_lag1',   # ✅ Granger-causes bed_occupancy (lagged for prediction models)
]

# Hospital KPI features (from 02_eda.ipynb analysis)
# Based on Granger causality tests:
#   - covid_patient_pct: ✅ Granger-causes bed_occupancy (lags 2,3,5,8)
#   - icu_occupancy_rate: ❌ Does NOT Granger-cause bed_occupancy
# FIXED: Use LAGGED KPI features to avoid data leakage in prediction models
# Note: VAR uses non-lagged covid_patient_pct as endogenous (forecasts jointly)
KPI_FEATURES = [
    'covid_patient_pct_lag1',   # ✅ Granger-causes bed_occupancy (lagged for prediction)
    'icu_occupancy_rate_lag1',  # For monitoring (lagged to avoid leakage)
]

# Non-lagged KPIs for VAR model (used as endogenous variables, not features)
KPI_FEATURES_VAR_ENDOGENOUS = [
    'covid_patient_pct',        # VAR forecasts this jointly with bed_occupancy
]

# External features (weather + flu) based on EDA correlation + multicollinearity analysis
# Selected to avoid redundancy while maximizing predictive power
EXTERNAL_FEATURES = [
    'ili',                      # r=0.387, p<0.0001 - STRONG (best flu predictor, keep over wili/flu_activity_level)
    'temp_min',                 # r=-0.254, p=0.0003 - MODERATE (best weather predictor, keep over temp_avg/temp_max)
]

# Features to EXCLUDE (redundant or not significant based on EDA multicollinearity analysis)
EXCLUDE_FEATURES = [
    # Redundant flu features (highly correlated with ili, r ≈ 1.0)
    'wili',                     # Redundant with ili (r=1.00)
    'flu_activity_level',       # Redundant with ili (r=1.00)
    # Redundant temperature features (highly correlated with temp_min, r > 0.95)
    'temp_avg',                 # Redundant with temp_min (r=0.99)
    'temp_max',                 # Redundant with temp_min (r=0.95)
    # Not statistically significant (p > 0.05)
    'precipitation',            # p=0.076, not significant
    'wind_speed',               # p=0.909, not significant
    'pressure',                 # p=0.672, not significant
    'is_flu_season',            # p=0.205, not significant
]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MODEL-SPECIFIC FEATURE CONFIGURATIONS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ARIMAX/SARIMAX: Exogenous variables
# Based on EDA: ili and temp_min are the strongest non-redundant predictors
# FIXED: Use LAGGED external features to avoid data leakage
# (CDC ILI data has ~1-2 week reporting lag, so current week's ILI isn't available at prediction time)
ARIMAX_FEATURES = {
    # External + calendar - USE LAGGED VERSIONS to avoid leakage
    'exogenous': ['ili_lag_1', 'temp_min_lag_1', 'holidays_in_week'],
    # Cyclical encodings for seasonality (annual + quarterly) - these are calendar-based, no leakage
    'cyclical': ['quarter_sin', 'quarter_cos', 'day_of_year_sin', 'day_of_year_cos'],
    # Granger-causal KPI lag (avoids leakage)
    'kpi_lagged': ['covid_patient_pct_lag1'],
}

# Random Forest: All features (can handle multicollinearity)
RANDOM_FOREST_FEATURES = {
    'critical': CRITICAL_FEATURES,
    'high_priority': HIGH_PRIORITY_FEATURES,
    'kpi': KPI_FEATURES,
    'max_features': 15,
    'corr_threshold': 0.90,
    'min_importance': 0.05,
}

# LSTM: Lag features + rolling stats + external (sequential model)
LSTM_FEATURES = {
    'critical': CRITICAL_FEATURES,
    'high_priority': HIGH_PRIORITY_FEATURES,
    'kpi': KPI_FEATURES,
    'max_features': 15,
    'corr_threshold': 0.95,  # Higher tolerance for neural networks
    'min_importance': 0.10,
}

# VAR: Multivariate endogenous + exogenous
# Based on 02_eda.ipynb Granger causality tests:
#   - covid_patient_pct Granger-causes bed_occupancy (significant at lags 2,3,5,8) ✅
#   - icu_occupancy_rate does NOT Granger-cause bed_occupancy ❌
# Stationarity (VAR requires stationary series):
#   - bed_occupancy: NON-STATIONARY → needs differencing
#   - covid_patient_pct: STATIONARY → no differencing needed
# NOTE: For VAR ENDOGENOUS variables, use NON-LAGGED versions because VAR
#       automatically handles lagging (it's autoregressive). Pre-lagging would add extra lag.
#       For EXOGENOUS variables (VARMAX), use lagged versions to avoid leakage.
VAR_FEATURES = {
    'endogenous_primary': ['bed_occupancy', 'covid_patient_pct'],  # Based on Granger causality
    'endogenous_fallback': ['bed_occupancy', 'ili', 'temp_min'],  # If KPIs unavailable (NON-lagged for VAR)
    'exogenous': ['quarter_sin', 'quarter_cos', 'day_of_year_sin', 'day_of_year_cos', 'ili_lag_1', 'temp_min_lag_1'],  # Lagged for VARMAX
    'max_lags': 4,  # Reduced from 8 for more adaptability (shorter memory)
    'ic': 'bic',    # BIC for simpler, more adaptive models (penalizes complexity)
    'trend': 'n',   # No trend for more variability in forecasts
    'differencing': {'bed_occupancy': 1, 'covid_patient_pct': 0},  # Based on stationarity tests
}

# Baseline models: Simple features only
BASELINE_FEATURES = {
    'naive': [],  # No features needed
    'seasonal_naive': ['week_of_year'],
    'moving_average': ['rolling_mean_4', 'rolling_mean_13'],
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FEATURE SELECTION PARAMETERS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
FEATURE_SELECTION_CONFIG = {
    'max_features_default': 15,
    'corr_threshold_default': 0.90,
    'min_importance_default': 0.05,
    'use_mutual_information': True,
    'corr_weight': 0.6,  # Weight for correlation in combined importance
    'mi_weight': 0.4,    # Weight for mutual information in combined importance
}

# Compile all configurations into a single dictionary for export
FEATURE_CONFIG = {
    'critical_features': CRITICAL_FEATURES,
    'high_priority_features': HIGH_PRIORITY_FEATURES,
    'kpi_features': KPI_FEATURES,
    'external_features': EXTERNAL_FEATURES,
    'exclude_features': EXCLUDE_FEATURES,
    'arimax': ARIMAX_FEATURES,
    'random_forest': RANDOM_FOREST_FEATURES,
    'lstm': LSTM_FEATURES,
    'var': VAR_FEATURES,
    'baseline': BASELINE_FEATURES,
    'selection_config': FEATURE_SELECTION_CONFIG,
}

print("\n📊 Feature Configuration Summary:")
print(f"   Critical features: {len(CRITICAL_FEATURES)}")
print(f"   High priority features: {len(HIGH_PRIORITY_FEATURES)}")
print(f"   KPI features: {len(KPI_FEATURES)}")
print(f"   External features: {len(EXTERNAL_FEATURES)}")
print(f"   Excluded features: {len(EXCLUDE_FEATURES)}")
print("\n   Model-specific configs defined for: ARIMAX, Random Forest, LSTM, VAR, Baseline")
print("="*70)

Load Weekly Time Series Data¶

In [ ]:
# Load weekly bed occupancy time series from previous notebook
# This loads weekly_occupancy.csv created in 01b_data_preprocessing.ipynb
# Data is from COVID-19 Hospital Capacity dataset for ADVENTHEALTH ORLANDO
# Try loading from multiple locations (priority: local > drive, matching notebook 02)
file_paths = [
    (DATA_PROCESSED, 'weekly_occupancy.csv'),
    (DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED, 'weekly_occupancy.csv') if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED else None
]

weekly_occupancy = pd.DataFrame()
for path_info in file_paths:
    if path_info is None:
        continue
    folder, filename = path_info
    file_path = os.path.join(folder, filename)
    if os.path.exists(file_path):
        try:
            weekly_occupancy = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
            print(f"✓ Loaded {len(weekly_occupancy):,} weeks from {file_path}")
            print(f"  (Weekly bed occupancy data from COVID-19 Hospital Capacity dataset)")
            print(f"Date range: {weekly_occupancy.index.min()} to {weekly_occupancy.index.max()}")
            print(f"  (Note: Real calendar dates from 2020-2024)")

            # ============================================================
            # DATA FILTERING: OPTIMAL TRAINING PERIOD
            # ============================================================
            # Based on exploratory analysis, filter to optimal training period (2020-2024)
            # This excludes low-activity periods with data quality concerns
            # The peak/plateau phase (2020-2024) is the most stable, high-activity period
            FILTER_TO_OPTIMAL_PERIOD = False  # Set to False to use all data

            if FILTER_TO_OPTIMAL_PERIOD:
                optimal_start = pd.Timestamp('2020-07-26')
                optimal_end = pd.Timestamp('2024-04-21')
                original_len = len(weekly_occupancy)
                weekly_occupancy = weekly_occupancy[
                    (weekly_occupancy.index >= optimal_start) &
                    (weekly_occupancy.index <= optimal_end)
                ]
                filtered_len = len(weekly_occupancy)
                print(f"\n📊 Data Filtering (Optimal Training Period):")
                print(f"  Original data: {original_len:,} weeks")
                print(f"  Filtered to optimal period (2020-2024): {filtered_len:,} weeks")
                print(f"  Removed: {original_len - filtered_len:,} weeks ({100*(original_len-filtered_len)/original_len:.1f}%)")
                print(f"  New date range: {weekly_occupancy.index.min()} to {weekly_occupancy.index.max()}")
            else:
                print(f"\n📊 Using all data (no filtering applied)")

            print(f"\nFirst few rows:")
            print(weekly_occupancy.head())
            break
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Error loading {file_path}: {e}")

if len(weekly_occupancy) == 0:
    print("❌ Data file not found. Please run notebook 02_exploratory_analysis.ipynb first.")
    print(f"   Checked locations:")
    for path_info in file_paths:
        if path_info:
            print(f"     - {os.path.join(path_info[0], path_info[1])}")

# ============================================================
# TRAIN/TEST SPLIT (Based on EDA Insights)
# ============================================================
# Split data chronologically by COMPLETE YEARS to preserve temporal order
# Test set should contain only complete years for clean evaluation
# COVID data spans 2020-2024 (196 weeks)
# Split: Use 80% for training, 20% for testing (chronological)

if len(weekly_occupancy) > 0:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("📊 TRAIN/TEST SPLIT (By Complete Years)")
    print("="*60)

    # Get unique years in the data
    available_years = sorted(weekly_occupancy.index.year.unique())
    total_weeks = len(weekly_occupancy)

    print(f"\nAvailable years in data: {available_years}")
    print(f"  Total weeks: {total_weeks:,}")

    # Split by complete years: Use last year(s) for test, rest for train
    # For COVID data (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024):
    #   Train: 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 (4 years)
    #   Test: 2024 (1 year) = ~20% by years

    test_years = [available_years[-1]]  # Last year for test
    train_years = available_years[:-1]  # All other years for train

    print(f"\nSplit by complete years:")
    print(f"  Train years: {train_years} ({len(train_years)} complete years)")
    print(f"  Test years: {test_years} ({len(test_years)} complete years)")

    # Split data by years
    train_data = weekly_occupancy[weekly_occupancy.index.year.isin(train_years)].copy()
    test_data = weekly_occupancy[weekly_occupancy.index.year.isin(test_years)].copy()

    print(f"\nSplit Configuration:")
    print(f"  Total weeks: {total_weeks:,}")
    print(f"  Train/Test by years: {len(train_years)} / {len(test_years)} years")
    print(f"  Train/Test by weeks: {len(train_data):,} / {len(test_data):,} weeks ({len(train_data)/total_weeks:.1%} / {len(test_data)/total_weeks:.1%})")

    print(f"\nTrain Set (Complete Years Only):")
    print(f"  Years: {train_years}")
    print(f"  Size: {len(train_data):,} weeks ({len(train_data)/total_weeks:.1%})")
    print(f"  Date range: {train_data.index.min().date()} to {train_data.index.max().date()}")
    train_year_counts = train_data.index.year.value_counts().sort_index()
    print(f"  Weeks per year: {dict(train_year_counts)}")
    print(f"  Mean bed occupancy: {train_data['bed_occupancy'].mean():.2f}")
    print(f"  Std bed occupancy: {train_data['bed_occupancy'].std():.2f}")

    print(f"\nTest Set (Complete Years Only):")
    print(f"  Years: {test_years}")
    print(f"  Size: {len(test_data):,} weeks ({len(test_data)/total_weeks:.1%})")
    print(f"  Date range: {test_data.index.min().date()} to {test_data.index.max().date()}")
    test_year_counts = test_data.index.year.value_counts().sort_index()
    print(f"  Weeks per year: {dict(test_year_counts)}")
    print(f"  Mean bed occupancy: {test_data['bed_occupancy'].mean():.2f}")
    print(f"  Std bed occupancy: {test_data['bed_occupancy'].std():.2f}")

    # Verify test set has complete seasonal cycles
    test_weeks = len(test_data)
    test_full_years = len(test_years)
    print(f"\n✅ Test Set Validation:")
    print(f"  Test set contains {test_full_years} complete year(s) ({test_weeks} weeks)")
    if test_weeks >= 52:
        print(f"  ✓ Test set has sufficient time span for seasonal pattern evaluation")
        if test_full_years == 1:
            print(f"  ✓ Test set contains exactly 1 complete year (ideal for yearly seasonality)")
    else:
        print(f"  ⚠️  Warning: Test set may be too short to capture full seasonal patterns")

    print(f"\n✅ Split Summary:")
    print(f"  ✓ Split by complete years (no partial years)")
    print(f"  ✓ Chronological split (preserves temporal order)")
    print(f"  ✓ Train set: {len(train_years)} complete years ({len(train_data):,} weeks)")
    print(f"  ✓ Test set: {len(test_years)} complete year(s) ({len(test_data):,} weeks)")

    # Store split indices for later use in feature engineering
    # Features will be created on full dataset, then split using these indices
    split_point_index = train_data.index[-1]
    print(f"\n  Split point: {split_point_index.date()} (end of last training year)")
    print(f"  (Last training week: {split_point_index.date()}, First test week: {test_data.index[0].date()})")
else:
    train_data = pd.DataFrame()
    test_data = pd.DataFrame()
    split_point_index = None
    print("⚠️  No data available for train/test split")

Load External Features (EDA-Driven Selection)¶

Based on correlation analysis from 02_eda.ipynb, load and select external features:

Strong Predictors (p < 0.0001):

  • ili - ILI rate (r = 0.387) - strongest flu predictor
  • temp_min - Minimum temperature (r = -0.254) - strongest weather predictor

Excluded (redundant or not significant):

  • flu_activity_level, wili - Redundant with ili (r ≈ 1.0 correlation)
  • temp_avg, temp_max - Redundant with temp_min (r > 0.95)
  • precipitation, wind_speed, pressure - Not statistically significant
  • is_flu_season - Not statistically significant (p = 0.20)

# EDA-based feature selection (updated)
# Strong predictors (p < 0.0001): ili
# Moderate predictors (p < 0.05): temp_min
# Excluded: flu_activity_level/wili (redundant with ili), temp_avg/max (redundant with temp_min),
#           precipitation/wind_speed/pressure/is_flu_season (not significant)
SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES = ['ili', 'temp_min']

external_file_paths = [
    (DATA_PROCESSED, 'weekly_occupancy_with_external.csv'),

]

for path_info in external_file_paths:

if len(external_data) > 0:
    # Check which selected features are available
    available_external = [col for col in SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES if col in external_data.columns]
    missing_external = [col for col in SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES if col not in external_data.columns]

    print(f"\n📋 EDA-Based Feature Selection:")
    print(f"  Strong predictors selected: ili (r=0.490), flu_activity_level (r=0.385)")
    print(f"  Moderate predictor selected: temp_avg (r=-0.221)")
    print(f"  Excluded (redundant): wili, temp_min, temp_max")
    print(f"  Excluded (not significant): precipitation, wind_speed, pressure")

    print(f"\n📊 Feature Availability:")
    print(f"  Available: {available_external}")
    if missing_external:
        print(f"  Missing: {missing_external}")

    # Extract selected features and store for later use

        external_features_df = external_data[available_external].copy()

        # Check for missing values

else:

Create Temporal Features¶

In [ ]:
# Create temporal features
# Note: Features are created on the full dataset, then split using train/test indices
# This ensures consistent feature engineering for both train and test sets
# IMPORTANT: This is WEEKLY data (all Sundays), so day-of-week features are constant
if len(weekly_occupancy) > 0:
    features_df = weekly_occupancy.copy()
    features_df['week_of_year'] = features_df.index.isocalendar().week
    features_df['week_of_year_name'] = features_df.index.strftime('%W')
    features_df['month'] = features_df.index.month
    features_df['month_name'] = features_df.index.month_name()
    features_df['quarter'] = features_df.index.quarter
    features_df['year'] = features_df.index.year

    # REMOVED: is_weekend (always 1 for weekly Sunday data - constant/useless)
    # REMOVED: is_month_start (rarely true for Sundays - only if Sunday falls on 1st)
    # REMOVED: is_month_end (rarely true for Sundays - only if Sunday falls on last day)

    # Additional temporal features
    # REMOVED: day_of_year (raw value - less granular for weekly data, only ~52 values/year)
    # KEPT: day_of_year_sin/cos (cyclical encoding is useful for annual seasonality)
    features_df['week_of_month'] = ((features_df.index.day - 1) // 7) + 1  # Week within month (1-5)
    features_df['is_quarter_start'] = features_df.index.is_quarter_start.astype(int)
    features_df['is_quarter_end'] = features_df.index.is_quarter_end.astype(int)

    # Note about weekly data
    print("Note: Data is WEEKLY (all Sundays). Day-of-week features will be constant:")

    # ============================================================
    # CYCLICAL ENCODING (UPDATED BASED ON EDA)
    # ============================================================
    # REMOVED: week_of_year_sin/cos (day-of-week effect too weak for weekly data)
    # REMOVED: month_sin/cos (monthly effect too weak for weekly data)
    # KEPT: day_of_year_sin/cos (annual seasonality is important: seasonal strength 0.188, moderate patterns)
    # ADDED: quarter_sin/cos (quarterly seasonality)

    # Day of year cyclical encoding (using dayofyear directly, not stored as feature)
    # This captures annual seasonality which is more important than weekly/monthly
    # For weekly data, we use the day of year of the Sunday date for cyclical encoding
    max_day_of_year = 366  # Account for leap years
    day_of_year_values = features_df.index.dayofyear  # Calculate but don't store as feature
    features_df['day_of_year_sin'] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * day_of_year_values / max_day_of_year)
    features_df['day_of_year_cos'] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * day_of_year_values / max_day_of_year)

    # Quarterly cyclical encoding (alternative to monthly - more meaningful)
    features_df['quarter_sin'] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * features_df['quarter'] / 4)
    features_df['quarter_cos'] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * features_df['quarter'] / 4)

    # ============================================================
    # ADDITIONAL INTERACTION FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # Interaction features capture combined effects of multiple variables
    print("\nCreating interaction features...")

    # REMOVED: Day-of-week interactions (day-of-week effect too weak)
    # REMOVED: Monthly interactions (monthly effect too weak)
    # KEPT: Quarterly and weekend interactions (more meaningful)

    # REMOVED: weekend_quarter_interaction (is_weekend always 1, so equals quarter - redundant)
    # REMOVED: quarter_doy_interaction (day_of_year removed, less meaningful for weekly data)

    print("  ✓ Interaction features created:")
    print("    - (Removed: weekend_quarter_interaction, quarter_doy_interaction - not useful for weekly data)")
    print("\n  Note: Removed day-of-week and monthly interactions (effects too weak per EDA)")

    print("\nTemporal features created (updated for weekly data):")
    print("  - Removed: is_weekend (always 1), is_month_start/end (rarely true), day_of_year (raw value)")
    print("  - Kept: quarter, week_of_month, is_quarter_start/end, day_of_year_sin/cos (cyclical encoding)")
    print(features_df[['bed_occupancy', 'quarter', 'week_of_month', 'day_of_year_sin', 'day_of_year_cos']].head(10))

Create Holiday Features¶

In [ ]:
# Add US federal holidays
# Note: COVID-19 Hospital Capacity dates are real calendar dates (2020-2024), but holidays library works for any year
# We'll adjust dates by subtracting ~100 years to check holidays, preserving variable holidays (e.g., Thanksgiving)
if len(features_df) > 0:
    # Calculate the date shift (approximately 100 years)
    date_shift_years = 0  # No date shift needed for COVID data  # Shift to year 2000 range

    # Get holidays for the adjusted year range
    adjusted_min_year = features_df.index.min().year - date_shift_years
    adjusted_max_year = features_df.index.max().year - date_shift_years
    us_holidays = holidays.UnitedStates(years=range(adjusted_min_year, adjusted_max_year + 1))

    # For weekly data, only create holidays_in_week (counts holidays in ±3 day window)
    # NOTE: For WEEKLY data (all Sundays), checking if the exact date is a holiday is not useful
    # Most holidays don't fall on Sundays. Instead, we use holidays_in_week to capture
    # whether there's a holiday within the week (±3 days), which is more appropriate for weekly forecasting.
    features_df['holidays_in_week'] = features_df.index.to_series().apply(
        lambda x: sum([(x + pd.Timedelta(days=i) - pd.DateOffset(years=date_shift_years)).date() in us_holidays
                      for i in range(-3, 4)])
    )

    # REMOVED: is_holiday (not useful for weekly data where dates are all Sundays)
    # REMOVED: is_holiday_weekend (depends on is_holiday, so not useful)

    print(f"Holiday features created (weekly data optimized):")
    print(f"  - holidays_in_week: Count of holidays in ±3 day window (appropriate for weekly data)")
    print(f"  - Total weeks with holidays: {(features_df['holidays_in_week'] > 0).sum()}")
    print(f"  - Max holidays in a week: {features_df['holidays_in_week'].max()}")
    print(f"  ⚠️  Removed: is_holiday, is_holiday_weekend (not useful for weekly Sunday data)")

Add External Features and Differencing¶

EDA Findings Applied:

  1. External Features: Add ili, flu_activity_level, temp_avg (significant predictors)
  2. Differencing: Data is non-stationary (ADF p=0.21), add differenced features for ARIMA models
  3. Lagged External Features: Add lags of external features for predictive modeling
In [ ]:
# ============================================================
# ADD EXTERNAL FEATURES AND DIFFERENCING (EDA-DRIVEN)
# ============================================================
# Based on 02_eda.ipynb findings:
# - External features: ili (r=0.490), flu_activity_level (r=0.385), temp_avg (r=-0.221)
# - Data is non-stationary: ADF p=0.21, KPSS p=0.01 → differencing needed

if len(features_df) > 0:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("📊 ADDING EXTERNAL FEATURES AND DIFFERENCING")
    print("="*60)

    # ============================================================
    # 1. MERGE EXTERNAL FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    if 'EXTERNAL_FEATURES_AVAILABLE' in dir() and EXTERNAL_FEATURES_AVAILABLE and len(external_features_df) > 0:
        print("\n1. Merging External Features (EDA-selected):")

        # Align external features with features_df index
        external_aligned = external_features_df.reindex(features_df.index)

        # Add only the SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES (avoid redundant/weak predictors)
        for col in SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES:
            if col in external_aligned.columns:
                features_df[col] = external_aligned[col]
                missing = features_df[col].isnull().sum()
                pct = missing / len(features_df) * 100
                print(f"   ✓ Added {col}: {missing} missing ({pct:.1f}%)")

        # Create lagged external features for predictive modeling
        print("\n   Creating lagged external features...")
        for col in SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES:
            if col in features_df.columns:
                # Lag 1: Previous week's value
                features_df[f'{col}_lag_1'] = features_df[col].shift(1)
                # Lag 4: Previous month's value (for seasonal patterns)
                features_df[f'{col}_lag_4'] = features_df[col].shift(4)
                print(f"   ✓ Added {col}_lag_1, {col}_lag_4")

        print(f"\n   ✓ External features merged: {len(SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES)} base + {len(SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES)*2} lagged")
    else:
        print("\n1. External Features: Not available (skipping)")

    # ============================================================
    # 2. DIFFERENCING FEATURES (for stationarity)
    # ============================================================
    # EDA showed non-stationary data (ADF p=0.21, KPSS p=0.01)
    # Add differenced features for ARIMA models
    print("\n2. Creating Differencing Features (stationarity):")
    print("   EDA finding: Non-stationary (ADF p=0.21, KPSS p=0.01)")
    print("   Solution: Add differenced features for ARIMA models")

    # First difference (d=1)
    # FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage - diff features should use past values only
    # These are for ARIMA model diagnostics/stationarity analysis, not as prediction features
    # diff_1[t] = occupancy[t-1] - occupancy[t-2] (past week's change)
    lagged_occupancy = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)
    features_df['bed_occupancy_diff_1'] = lagged_occupancy.diff(1)
    print("   ✓ Added bed_occupancy_diff_1 (lagged first difference - no leakage)")

    # Seasonal difference (52 weeks for annual seasonality)
    if len(features_df) >= 52:
        features_df['bed_occupancy_diff_52'] = lagged_occupancy.diff(52)
        print("   ✓ Added bed_occupancy_diff_52 (lagged seasonal difference - no leakage)")

    # Second difference (for trend removal if needed)
    features_df['bed_occupancy_diff_2'] = lagged_occupancy.diff(1).diff(1)
    print("   ✓ Added bed_occupancy_diff_2 (lagged second difference - no leakage)")

    # Differenced external features (if available)
    if 'EXTERNAL_FEATURES_AVAILABLE' in dir() and EXTERNAL_FEATURES_AVAILABLE:
        print("\n   Creating differenced external features...")
        for col in SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES:
            if col in features_df.columns:
                features_df[f'{col}_diff_1'] = features_df[col].diff(1)
                print(f"   ✓ Added {col}_diff_1")

    # ============================================================
    # 3. SUMMARY
    # ============================================================
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("📊 EXTERNAL FEATURES AND DIFFERENCING SUMMARY")
    print("="*60)

    external_cols = [col for col in features_df.columns if any(x in col for x in ['ili', 'flu_activity', 'temp_avg'])]
    diff_cols = [col for col in features_df.columns if '_diff_' in col]

    print(f"  External features added: {len(external_cols)}")
    print(f"  Differencing features added: {len(diff_cols)}")
    print(f"  Total columns in features_df: {len(features_df.columns)}")

    if external_cols:
        print(f"\n  External feature columns: {external_cols}")
    if diff_cols:
        print(f"  Differencing columns: {diff_cols}")

    print("="*60)

Create Lag Features¶

EDA-Based Lag Selection (from ACF/PACF analysis):

  • Lag 1: Strongest autocorrelation (r = 0.898)
  • Lag 3: PACF significant
  • Lag 4: PACF significant (monthly pattern in weekly data)
  • Lag 52: Annual seasonality
In [ ]:
# Create lagged features (previous weeks)
# UPDATED BASED ON EDA: Lag selection driven by ACF/PACF analysis
# - ACF shows strong autocorrelation at lag 1 (r = 0.898)
# - PACF shows significant values at lags 1, 3, 4, 10, 14
# - 52-week seasonality detected
# Note: NaN values at start are EXPECTED - first N rows have no previous data to reference
# These NaN rows will be removed in the cleaning step below
if len(features_df) > 0:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("📊 CREATING LAG FEATURES (EDA-DRIVEN)")
    print("="*60)
    print("Based on ACF/PACF analysis from 02_eda.ipynb:")
    print("  - Lag 1: Strongest autocorrelation (r = 0.898)")
    print("  - Lag 3: PACF significant")
    print("  - Lag 4: PACF significant (monthly pattern in weekly data)")
    print("  - Lag 52: Annual seasonality")

    # Lag 1: Previous week (strongest autocorrelation)
    features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)

    # Lag 3: PACF significant - captures short-term momentum
    features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_3'] = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(3)

    # Lag 4: PACF significant - monthly pattern (4 weeks ≈ 1 month)
    features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_4'] = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(4)

    # Lag 52: Year-over-year (annual seasonality)
    # Important for hospital bed occupancy which have strong annual patterns
    if len(features_df) >= 52:
        features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_52'] = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(52)

    print("\n✓ Lag features created based on ACF/PACF analysis:")
    print("  - bed_occupancy_lag_1 (strongest autocorrelation)")
    print("  - bed_occupancy_lag_3 (PACF significant)")
    print("  - bed_occupancy_lag_4 (monthly pattern)")
    if len(features_df) >= 52:
        print("  - bed_occupancy_lag_52 (annual seasonality)")

    # ============================================================
    # LAG-TEMPORAL INTERACTION FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # These capture conditional effects (e.g., weekend lag patterns differ from weekday)
    # NOTE: For weekly data (all Sundays), weekend interactions will be constant
    print("\nCreating lag-temporal interaction features...")

    interaction_features_created = []

    # REMOVED: Lag 1 × Weekend interaction (is_weekend always 1 for weekly data, so equals lag_1 - redundant)

    # REMOVED: Lag 1 × Holiday interaction (is_holiday feature removed - not useful for weekly data)

    # Lag 52 × Quarter: Year-over-year effect may vary by season/quarter
    if 'bed_occupancy_lag_52' in features_df.columns and 'quarter' in features_df.columns:
        features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_52_quarter'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_52'] * features_df['quarter']
        interaction_features_created.append('bed_occupancy_lag_52_quarter')

    if interaction_features_created:
        # Remove duplicates from list
        interaction_features_created = list(dict.fromkeys(interaction_features_created))
        print(f"  ✓ Created {len(interaction_features_created)} lag-temporal interaction features:")
        for feat in interaction_features_created:
            print(f"    - {feat}")
        print(f"\n  📊 Validation: Sample values for interaction features:")
        interaction_cols = ['bed_occupancy'] + interaction_features_created[:3]  # Show first 3
        if all(col in features_df.columns for col in interaction_cols):
            print(features_df[interaction_cols].head(5))
    else:
        print("  ⚠️  No lag-temporal interaction features created (missing required base features)")

    lag_cols = ['bed_occupancy', 'bed_occupancy_lag_1', 'bed_occupancy_lag_4']
    if 'bed_occupancy_lag_52' in features_df.columns:
        lag_cols.append('bed_occupancy_lag_52')
    print(f"\n📊 Lag Features Preview:")
    print(features_df[lag_cols].head(10))

# ============================================================
# POLYNOMIAL/INTERACTION FEATURES
# ============================================================
# Create interaction terms between key features to capture non-linear relationships
# Only create interaction terms (not squares) to avoid feature explosion
# Focus on interactions between high-importance features
# NOTE: Some features (rolling stats) are created in later cells, so some interactions
#       may not be created here. They can be added later if needed.

if len(features_df) > 0:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("🔗 CREATING POLYNOMIAL/INTERACTION FEATURES")
    print("="*60)
    print("Purpose: Capture non-linear relationships between key features")
    print("Note: Rolling stat interactions will be created after rolling stats cell")

    interaction_features_created = []

    # Key features for interactions (high importance features)
    # FIXED: Removed duplicate dictionary keys
    key_features = {
        'bed_occupancy_lag_1': 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns,
        'bed_occupancy_lag_3': 'bed_occupancy_lag_3' in features_df.columns,
        'bed_occupancy_lag_4': 'bed_occupancy_lag_4' in features_df.columns,
        'bed_occupancy_lag_52': 'bed_occupancy_lag_52' in features_df.columns,
        'rolling_mean_4': 'rolling_mean_4' in features_df.columns,
        'rolling_median_4': 'rolling_median_4' in features_df.columns,
        'bed_occupancy_rate': 'bed_occupancy_rate' in features_df.columns,
        'capacity_zone': 'capacity_zone' in features_df.columns,
        # 'is_weekend': removed (always 1 for weekly data)
        'quarter': 'quarter' in features_df.columns,
        # 'day_of_year': removed (raw value, keep sin/cos only)
    }

    available_features = {k: v for k, v in key_features.items() if v}
    print(f"  Available base features: {[k for k, v in available_features.items() if v]}")

    # 1. Lag × Rolling Statistics interactions (will be skipped if rolling stats not yet created)
    if available_features.get('bed_occupancy_lag_1') and available_features.get('rolling_mean_4'):
        features_df['lag1_x_rolling_mean_4'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] * features_df['rolling_mean_4']
        interaction_features_created.append('lag1_x_rolling_mean_4')

    if available_features.get('bed_occupancy_lag_1') and available_features.get('rolling_median_4'):
        features_df['lag1_x_rolling_median_4'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] * features_df['rolling_median_4']
        interaction_features_created.append('lag1_x_rolling_median_4')

    # 2. Lag squared (captures non-linear lag effects)
    if available_features.get('bed_occupancy_lag_1'):
        features_df['lag1_squared'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] ** 2
        interaction_features_created.append('lag1_squared')

    # 3. Capacity × Lag interactions (capacity constraints affect occupancy patterns)
    if available_features.get('capacity_zone') and available_features.get('bed_occupancy_lag_1'):
        features_df['capacity_zone_x_lag1'] = features_df['capacity_zone'] * features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1']
        interaction_features_created.append('capacity_zone_x_lag1')

    # 4. Temporal × Lag interactions (seasonal variations in lag effects)
    if available_features.get('quarter') and available_features.get('bed_occupancy_lag_52'):
        features_df['quarter_x_lag52'] = features_df['quarter'] * features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_52']
        interaction_features_created.append('quarter_x_lag52')

    # REMOVED: day_of_year × lag_52 interaction (day_of_year removed - less meaningful for weekly data)

    # 5. Rolling Statistics × Capacity interactions (will be skipped if not available)
    if available_features.get('rolling_mean_4') and available_features.get('capacity_zone'):
        features_df['rolling_mean4_x_capacity_zone'] = features_df['rolling_mean_4'] * features_df['capacity_zone']
        interaction_features_created.append('rolling_mean4_x_capacity_zone')

    if interaction_features_created:
        print(f"\n✅ Created {len(interaction_features_created)} polynomial/interaction features:")
        for feat in interaction_features_created:
            print(f"    - {feat}")

        # Validation: Show sample statistics
        print(f"\n📊 Validation - Sample Statistics for Interaction Features:")
        interaction_cols = [col for col in interaction_features_created if col in features_df.columns]
        if interaction_cols:
            sample_stats = features_df[interaction_cols].describe().T[['mean', 'std', 'min', 'max']]
            print(sample_stats)
    else:
        print("  ⚠️  No polynomial/interaction features created (missing required base features)")
        print("  Note: Rolling stats are created in a later cell. Some interactions may be added there.")

    print("="*60 + "\n")

Create Rolling Statistics¶

In [ ]:
# Create rolling window statistics
# Note: NaN values at start are EXPECTED until the rolling window is filled
# Example: rolling_mean_4 has NaN for first 3 weeks (need 4 weeks to calculate mean)
# FIXED: Use .shift(1) BEFORE rolling to avoid data leakage (current target value in rolling window)
if len(features_df) > 0:
    # Create lagged series to avoid data leakage - rolling stats should only use PAST values
    lagged_occupancy = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)

    # 4-week rolling statistics (approximately 1 month for weekly data)
    features_df['rolling_mean_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4, center=False).mean()
    features_df['rolling_std_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4, center=False).std()
    features_df['rolling_min_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4, center=False).min()
    features_df['rolling_max_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4, center=False).max()
    features_df['rolling_median_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4, center=False).median()

    # 13-week rolling statistics (approximately 1 quarter for weekly data)
    if len(features_df) > 13:
        features_df['rolling_mean_13'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13, center=False).mean()
        features_df['rolling_std_13'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13, center=False).std()
        features_df['rolling_median_13'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13, center=False).median()

    # 52-week rolling statistics (annual trend)
    if len(features_df) > 52:
        features_df['rolling_mean_52'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=52, center=False).mean()
        features_df['rolling_median_52'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=52, center=False).median()

    print("Rolling statistics created (NaN at start is expected - will be removed later):")
    print(f"  - 4-week: rolling_mean_4, rolling_std_4, rolling_min_4, rolling_max_4, rolling_median_4")
    if len(features_df) > 13:
        print(f"  - 13-week: rolling_mean_13, rolling_std_13, rolling_median_13")
    if len(features_df) > 52:
        print(f"  - 52-week: rolling_mean_52, rolling_median_52")
    print(features_df[['bed_occupancy', 'rolling_mean_4', 'rolling_median_4']].head(10))

Create Domain-Specific Hospital Features¶

Hospital operational patterns: month-end/quarter-end effects, Monday spikes, etc.

In [ ]:
# ============================================================
# DOMAIN-SPECIFIC HOSPITAL FEATURES
# ============================================================
# Capture operational patterns specific to hospital environments:
# - Month-end/quarter-end discharge patterns (insurance cycles)
# - Monday spikes (post-weekend catch-up)
# - Friday lows (discharges before weekend)

if len(features_df) > 0:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("🏥 CREATING DOMAIN-SPECIFIC HOSPITAL FEATURES")
    print("="*60)
    print("Purpose: Capture operational patterns specific to hospital environments")

    domain_features_created = []

    # REMOVED: Month-end effects (days_to_month_end, near_month_end, is_last_3_days_of_month)
    # Reason: Less meaningful for weekly data - only 4-5 unique values per month
    # KEPT: is_first_week_of_month, is_last_week_of_month (more appropriate for weekly data)

    # REMOVED: Quarter-end effects (days_to_quarter_end, near_quarter_end, is_last_3_days_of_quarter)
    # Reason: Less meaningful for weekly data - only ~13 unique values per quarter
    # KEPT: is_quarter_end (boolean flag is more appropriate for weekly data)

    # REMOVED: Monday spike features (is_monday, monday_after_low_weekend)
    # Reason: Always 0 for weekly Sunday data - constant/useless

    # REMOVED: Friday low features (is_friday)
    # Reason: Always 0 for weekly Sunday data - constant/useless
    # REMOVED: Friday before long weekend features (depends on is_holiday which was removed)
    # REMOVED: next_monday_is_holiday (data leakage - uses .shift(-3) for future data)

    # 5. Seasonal transition periods (early spring, late fall - flu season transitions)
    month = features_df.index.month
    day = features_df.index.day
    features_df['early_spring'] = ((month == 3) & (day <= 15)).astype(int)
    features_df['late_fall'] = ((month == 11) & (day >= 15)).astype(int)
    domain_features_created.extend(['early_spring', 'late_fall'])

    # 6. First/last week of month (insurance and administrative patterns)
    week_of_month = ((features_df.index.day - 1) // 7) + 1
    # FIXED: Use .days_in_month directly on DatetimeIndex, not on PeriodIndex
    days_in_month = features_df.index.days_in_month
    max_week = ((days_in_month - 1) // 7) + 1
    features_df['is_first_week_of_month'] = (week_of_month == 1).astype(int)
    features_df['is_last_week_of_month'] = (week_of_month == max_week).astype(int)
    domain_features_created.extend(['is_first_week_of_month', 'is_last_week_of_month'])

    # Fill NaN values
    for col in domain_features_created:
        if col in features_df.columns:
            features_df[col] = features_df[col].fillna(0)

    print(f"\n✅ Created {len(domain_features_created)} domain-specific hospital features (weekly data optimized):")
    print(f"  - Quarter effects: {len([f for f in domain_features_created if 'quarter' in f])} features")
    print(f"  - Seasonal transitions: {len([f for f in domain_features_created if 'spring' in f or 'fall' in f])} features")
    print(f"  - Week-of-month patterns: {len([f for f in domain_features_created if 'week_of_month' in f])} features")
    print(f"  ⚠️  Removed: Month-end/Quarter-end day-based features, Monday/Friday features (not useful for weekly data)")

    # Show created features
    for feat in domain_features_created:
        print(f"    - {feat}")

    print("="*60 + "\n")

Create Change Features¶

In [ ]:
# Create change features (week-over-week for weekly data)
# These capture momentum and short-term trends
# FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage - change features should use past values only
if len(features_df) > 0:
    # Lagged series to calculate changes on past data (not including current target)
    lagged_occupancy = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)

    # Week-over-week change (1 week for weekly data)
    # This gives: change_1[t] = occupancy[t-1] - occupancy[t-2] (past week's change)
    features_df['bed_occupancy_change_1'] = lagged_occupancy.diff(1)  # Week-over-week change
    features_df['bed_occupancy_pct_change_1'] = lagged_occupancy.pct_change(1)  # Percentage change

    # Month-over-month change (4 weeks for weekly data)
    if len(features_df) > 4:
        features_df['bed_occupancy_change_4'] = lagged_occupancy.diff(4)
        features_df['bed_occupancy_pct_change_4'] = lagged_occupancy.pct_change(4)

    # Fill NaN values from change calculations with 0 (no change on first days)
    change_cols = [col for col in features_df.columns if 'change' in col]
    for col in change_cols:
        features_df[col] = features_df[col].fillna(0)

    print("Change features created:")
    print(features_df[['bed_occupancy', 'bed_occupancy_change_1', 'bed_occupancy_change_4', 'bed_occupancy_pct_change_1']].head(10))

    # ============================================================
    # TIME-BASED FEATURES (Days Since/Until Events)
    # ============================================================
    # These capture temporal proximity to important events
    print("\nCreating time-based features (days since/until events)...")

    # REMOVED: days_since_holiday (depends on is_holiday which was removed, also had high VIF: 22.53)
    # REMOVED: days_until_next_holiday (DATA LEAKAGE - uses future information)
    # REMOVED: days_since_weekend, days_until_weekend (redundant with week_of_year and is_weekend)
    # REMOVED: days_since_month_start, days_until_month_end (redundant with week_of_month)

    print("  ✓ Time-based features created:")
    print(f"    - Removed: days_since_holiday (depends on removed is_holiday, high VIF), days_until_next_holiday (data leakage)")
    print(f"    - Removed: days_since/until_weekend/month (redundant)")

    # ============================================================
    # ZERO-INFLATION FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # These features explicitly model zero or low-value patterns to help models distinguish between:
    # - Weeks with very low bed occupancy (predictable patterns)
    # - Weeks with normal bed occupancy
    # - Weeks with extreme bed occupancy (outliers)
    # NOTE: If using filtered period (2020-2024), zeros may not exist - features will be skipped
    print("\nCreating zero-inflation features (to handle zero-inflated distribution)...")

    # Check if zeros exist in the data (if filtered period has no zeros, skip these features)
    zeros_exist = (features_df['bed_occupancy'] == 0).sum() > 0
    if not zeros_exist:
        print("  ⚠️  No zeros found in data - skipping zero-inflation features")
        print("     (If using filtered period, zeros may have been removed)")
        print("     Zero-inflation features will not be created.")

    # Only create zero-inflation features if zeros exist in the data
    if zeros_exist:
        # 1. Zero indicators (was there a zero recently?)
        if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
            features_df['was_zero_yesterday'] = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] == 0).astype(int)
        if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
            features_df['was_zero_last_week'] = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] == 0).astype(int)
        if 'bed_occupancy_lag_52' in features_df.columns:
            features_df['was_zero_last_year'] = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_52'] == 0).astype(int)
    else:
        # Create empty placeholders (will be removed as constant features)
        if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
            features_df['was_zero_yesterday'] = 0
        if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
            features_df['was_zero_last_week'] = 0
        if 'bed_occupancy_lag_52' in features_df.columns:
            features_df['was_zero_last_year'] = 0

    # 2. Consecutive zeros (how many weeks in a row with zero bed occupancy?)
    # FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage
    # We calculate consecutive zeros based on yesterday's value, then shift forward
    if zeros_exist:
        features_df['consecutive_zeros'] = 0
        zero_count = 0
        for idx in features_df.index:
            # Use lag_1 to avoid data leakage (previous week's bed occupancy)
            if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
                lag_val = features_df.loc[idx, 'bed_occupancy_lag_1']
                if pd.notna(lag_val) and lag_val == 0:
                    zero_count += 1
                else:
                    zero_count = 0
            else:
                # If no lag_1, can't calculate (shouldn't happen)
                zero_count = 0
            features_df.loc[idx, 'consecutive_zeros'] = zero_count
    else:
        features_df['consecutive_zeros'] = 0

    # 3. Zero probability in rolling windows (proportion of zeros in recent period)
    # FIXED: Use lagged occupancy to avoid data leakage
    # FIXED: Use appropriate window sizes for weekly data (4w=month, 13w=quarter, 52w=year)
    # Calculate zero probability based on lagged values (excluding current week)
    if zeros_exist and 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
        # Use lag_1 for rolling calculations (excludes current week)
        # Apply lambda function to count zeros within each rolling window
        # 4-week window (approximately 1 month)
        features_df['prob_zero_4w'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].rolling(window=4).apply(
            lambda x: (x == 0).sum() / len(x) if len(x) > 0 else 0, raw=True
        )
        # 13-week window (approximately 1 quarter)
        if len(features_df) > 13:
            features_df['prob_zero_13w'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].rolling(window=13).apply(
                lambda x: (x == 0).sum() / len(x) if len(x) > 0 else 0, raw=True
            )
        # 52-week window (1 year)
        if len(features_df) > 52:
            features_df['prob_zero_52w'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].rolling(window=52).apply(
                lambda x: (x == 0).sum() / len(x) if len(x) > 0 else 0, raw=True
            )
    else:
        # No zeros in data - set to 0
        features_df['prob_zero_4w'] = 0
        if len(features_df) > 13:
            features_df['prob_zero_13w'] = 0
        if len(features_df) > 52:
            features_df['prob_zero_52w'] = 0

        # 4. Weeks since last non-zero bed occupancy
    # FIXED: Calculate based on lagged values, then shift forward to avoid data leakage
    # This captures how long it's been since the hospital had any bed occupancy (based on previous week's data)
    if zeros_exist:
        # We'll calculate for lagged values, then shift forward
        temp_days_since_nonzero = pd.Series(index=features_df.index, dtype=float)
        last_nonzero_idx = None
        for idx in features_df.index:
            # Use lag_1 to avoid data leakage
            if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
                lag_val = features_df.loc[idx, 'bed_occupancy_lag_1']
                if pd.notna(lag_val) and lag_val > 0:
                    last_nonzero_idx = idx
                    temp_days_since_nonzero.loc[idx] = 0
                elif last_nonzero_idx is not None:
                    days_since = (idx - last_nonzero_idx).days
                    temp_days_since_nonzero.loc[idx] = days_since
                else:
                    temp_days_since_nonzero.loc[idx] = 999  # No non-zero yet (at start of data)
            else:
                temp_days_since_nonzero.loc[idx] = 999

        # Shift forward by 1 day (yesterday's "days since nonzero" becomes today's feature)
        features_df['days_since_nonzero'] = temp_days_since_nonzero.shift(1).fillna(999)
    else:
        # No zeros - set to 0 (always have non-zero bed occupancy)
        features_df['days_since_nonzero'] = 0

    # 5. Count of zeros in rolling windows
    # FIXED: Use lagged occupancy to avoid data leakage
    # FIXED: Use appropriate window sizes for weekly data (4w=month, 13w=quarter)
    if zeros_exist and 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
        # 4-week window (approximately 1 month)
        features_df['zeros_count_4w'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].rolling(window=4).apply(
            lambda x: (x == 0).sum(), raw=True
        )
        # 13-week window (approximately 1 quarter)
        if len(features_df) > 13:
            features_df['zeros_count_13w'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].rolling(window=13).apply(
                lambda x: (x == 0).sum(), raw=True
            )
    else:
        # No zeros - set to 0
        features_df['zeros_count_4w'] = 0
        if len(features_df) > 13:
            features_df['zeros_count_13w'] = 0

        # 6. Extreme value indicators (for right tail - outliers)
    # Based on EDA: Some weeks with unusually high bed occupancy
    # Define extreme as > 30 (approximately 95th percentile based on distribution)
    # NOTE: These features are useful even without zeros (capture extreme high values)
    if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
        features_df['was_extreme_high_yesterday'] = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] > 30).astype(int)
    else:
        features_df['was_extreme_high_yesterday'] = 0

    if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
        features_df['was_extreme_high_last_week'] = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] > 30).astype(int)
    else:
        features_df['was_extreme_high_last_week'] = 0

    # Days since extreme high bed occupancy (recovery period)
    # FIXED: Calculate based on lagged values to avoid data leakage
    # Check if extreme values exist
    extreme_values_exist = False
    if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
        extreme_values_exist = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] > 30).sum() > 0

    if extreme_values_exist:
        temp_days_since_extreme = pd.Series(index=features_df.index, dtype=float)
        last_extreme_idx = None
        for idx in features_df.index:
            # Use lag_1 to avoid data leakage
            if 'bed_occupancy_lag_1' in features_df.columns:
                lag_val = features_df.loc[idx, 'bed_occupancy_lag_1']
                if pd.notna(lag_val) and lag_val > 30:
                    last_extreme_idx = idx
                    temp_days_since_extreme.loc[idx] = 0
                elif last_extreme_idx is not None:
                    days_since = (idx - last_extreme_idx).days
                    temp_days_since_extreme.loc[idx] = days_since
                else:
                    temp_days_since_extreme.loc[idx] = 999  # No extreme high yet
            else:
                temp_days_since_extreme.loc[idx] = 999

        # Shift forward by 1 day (yesterday's "days since extreme" becomes today's feature)
        features_df['days_since_extreme_high'] = temp_days_since_extreme.shift(1).fillna(999)
    else:
        # No extreme values - set to 999 (never had extreme high)
        features_df['days_since_extreme_high'] = 999

    # Fill NaN values from zero-inflation features
    # UPDATED: Use new feature names for weekly data
    zero_inflation_cols = [
        'was_zero_yesterday', 'was_zero_last_week', 'was_zero_last_year',
        'consecutive_zeros', 'prob_zero_4w', 'prob_zero_13w', 'prob_zero_52w',
        'days_since_nonzero', 'zeros_count_4w', 'zeros_count_13w',
        'was_extreme_high_yesterday', 'was_extreme_high_last_week', 'days_since_extreme_high'
    ]
    for col in zero_inflation_cols:
        if col in features_df.columns:
            features_df[col] = features_df[col].fillna(0)

    # Print summary
    created_cols = [col for col in zero_inflation_cols if col in features_df.columns]

    if zeros_exist:
        print("  ✓ Zero-inflation features created:")
        print(f"    - Zero indicators: was_zero_yesterday, was_zero_last_week, was_zero_last_year")
        print(f"    - Consecutive zeros: consecutive_zeros")
        print(f"    - Zero probability (weekly windows): prob_zero_4w, prob_zero_13w, prob_zero_52w")
        print(f"    - Days since non-zero: days_since_nonzero")
        print(f"    - Zero counts (weekly windows): zeros_count_4w, zeros_count_13w")
        print(f"    - Extreme value indicators: was_extreme_high_yesterday, was_extreme_high_last_week, days_since_extreme_high")
        print(f"    - Total zero-inflation features: {len(created_cols)}")
    else:
        print("  ⚠️  Zero-inflation features created but will be constant (no zeros in data):")
        print(f"    - Created {len(created_cols)} features (will be removed as constant)")
        print(f"    - Extreme value features may still be useful (was_extreme_high_*)")
        print(f"    - If using filtered period, zeros may have been removed")

# Add KPI features if available
# Try loading from multiple locations (matching notebook 02)
kpi_file_paths = [
    (DATA_PROCESSED, 'weekly_kpis.csv'),
    (DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED, 'weekly_kpis.csv') if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED else None
]

kpi_data = None
for path_info in kpi_file_paths:
    if path_info is None:
        continue
    folder, filename = path_info
    kpi_file = os.path.join(folder, filename)
    if os.path.exists(kpi_file):
        try:
            kpi_data = pd.read_csv(kpi_file, index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
            print(f"✓ Loaded KPI data from {kpi_file}")
            break
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Error loading {kpi_file}: {e}")

if kpi_data is not None and len(kpi_data) > 0:
    # Align KPI data with features_df index
    kpi_data = kpi_data.reindex(features_df.index)

    # ============================================================
    # NEW: CHECK FOR VAR MODEL KPIS (ICU, COVID)
    # ============================================================
    VAR_KPIS = ['icu_occupancy_rate', 'covid_patient_pct', 'icu_occupied',
                'icu_capacity', 'covid_inpatients', 'staffed_beds']
    available_var_kpis = [col for col in VAR_KPIS if col in kpi_data.columns]

    print("\n📊 VAR Model KPIs Check:")
    print(f"  Available KPIs: {list(kpi_data.columns)}")

    if available_var_kpis:
        print(f"\n  ✓ VAR KPIs available: {available_var_kpis}")
        for kpi in available_var_kpis:
            non_null = kpi_data[kpi].notna().sum()
            pct = 100 * non_null / len(kpi_data)
            print(f"    - {kpi}: {non_null}/{len(kpi_data)} non-null ({pct:.1f}%)")
    else:
        print(f"\n  ⚠️ No VAR KPIs available. Re-run 01b_data_preprocessing.ipynb to extract:")
        print(f"     {VAR_KPIS}")

    # ============================================================
    # CAPACITY CONSTRAINT FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # These features model when hospital is at or near capacity,
    # which can constrain occupancy or affect occupancy patterns

    # Check for bed occupancy column (may have different names)
    bed_occ_col = None
    if 'bed_occupancy_rate' in kpi_data.columns:
        bed_occ_col = 'bed_occupancy_rate'
    elif 'bed_occupancy' in kpi_data.columns:
        bed_occ_col = 'bed_occupancy'
    elif 'occupancy_rate' in kpi_data.columns:
        bed_occ_col = 'occupancy_rate'

    if bed_occ_col is not None:
        print("\n  Creating capacity constraint features from bed occupancy data...")

        # 1. Direct capacity indicators
        # FIXED: Use lagged bed_occupancy_rate to avoid data leakage
        # Current day's bed_occupancy may include same-day occupancy (leakage)
        # Yesterday's capacity affects today's occupancy (causal and no leakage)
        bed_occupancy_series = kpi_data[bed_occ_col]
        features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] = bed_occupancy_series.shift(1)

        # Also keep current for reference, but models should use lag_1
        features_df['bed_occupancy_rate'] = bed_occupancy_series

        # 2. Capacity threshold indicators (industry standard thresholds)
        # Use lagged occupancy for thresholds to avoid leakage
        # Near capacity: 85% (common threshold for operational alerts)
        features_df['near_capacity'] = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] >= 0.85).astype(int)

        # At capacity: 95% (critical threshold - may start diverting patients)
        features_df['at_capacity'] = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] >= 0.95).astype(int)

        # Over capacity: >100% (overflow situations - rare but critical)
        features_df['over_capacity'] = (features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] > 1.0).astype(int)

        # 3. Capacity zones (categorical encoding)
        # Low: <70%, Medium: 70-85%, High: 85-95%, Critical: >95%
        # Use lagged occupancy to avoid leakage
        def capacity_zone(rate):
            if pd.isna(rate):
                return 0
            elif rate < 0.70:
                return 1  # Low
            elif rate < 0.85:
                return 2  # Medium
            elif rate < 0.95:
                return 3  # High
            else:
                return 4  # Critical

        features_df['capacity_zone'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].apply(capacity_zone)

        # 4. Distance from capacity thresholds (using lagged occupancy)
        features_df['distance_from_85pct'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] - 0.85
        features_df['distance_from_95pct'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] - 0.95

        # 5. Additional lagged capacity features
        # bed_occupancy_lag_1 already created above (primary feature)
        features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_7'] = bed_occupancy_series.shift(1)
        features_df['near_capacity_lag_1'] = features_df['near_capacity']  # Already based on lag_1
        features_df['at_capacity_lag_1'] = features_df['at_capacity']  # Already based on lag_1

        # 6. Rolling capacity statistics (trend in capacity)
        # Use lagged occupancy for rolling stats to avoid leakage
        features_df['capacity_rolling_mean_4'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].rolling(window=4).mean()
        features_df['capacity_rolling_mean_4'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].rolling(window=4).mean()
        # Removed: capacity_rolling_max_4 (less informative than mean)

        # 7. Capacity change features (is capacity increasing/decreasing?)
        # Use lagged occupancy for changes
        features_df['capacity_change_1'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].diff(1)
        features_df['capacity_change_7'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'].diff(1)
        # Removed: capacity_pct_change_7 (may be redundant with capacity_change_7)

        # REMOVED: Interaction features: capacity × weekend
        # Reason: is_weekend always 1 for weekly data, so near_capacity_weekend equals near_capacity - redundant

        # 9. Days at high capacity (consecutive days near/at capacity)
        # This captures sustained capacity pressure
        # FIXED: Added data validation and cap to prevent unrealistic values
        features_df['days_near_capacity'] = 0
        features_df['days_at_capacity'] = 0

        # Check if bed occupancy data is valid (not constant/unrealistic)
        occupancy_valid = True
        if features_df['bed_occupancy_rate'].nunique() < 10:
            print("  ⚠️  Warning: Bed occupancy has very few unique values - data may be constant/aggregated")
            occupancy_valid = False

        # Check for unrealistic constant high occupancy
        high_occupancy_pct = (features_df['bed_occupancy_rate'] >= 0.85).sum() / len(features_df)
        if high_occupancy_pct > 0.95:
            print(f"  ⚠️  Warning: {high_occupancy_pct*100:.1f}% of days are near capacity - data may be unrealistic")
            occupancy_valid = False

        near_capacity_count = 0
        at_capacity_count = 0
        max_reasonable_days = 365  # Cap at 1 year (reasonable maximum)

        # Use lagged capacity indicators for consecutive days calculation
        for idx in features_df.index:
            # Use lagged near_capacity (already based on lag_1)
            if pd.notna(features_df.loc[idx, 'near_capacity']) and features_df.loc[idx, 'near_capacity'] == 1:
                near_capacity_count += 1
            else:
                near_capacity_count = 0
            # Cap at reasonable maximum to prevent unrealistic values
            features_df.loc[idx, 'days_near_capacity'] = min(near_capacity_count, max_reasonable_days)

            # Use lagged at_capacity (already based on lag_1)
            if pd.notna(features_df.loc[idx, 'at_capacity']) and features_df.loc[idx, 'at_capacity'] == 1:
                at_capacity_count += 1
            else:
                at_capacity_count = 0
            # Cap at reasonable maximum
            features_df.loc[idx, 'days_at_capacity'] = min(at_capacity_count, max_reasonable_days)

        # Report if values were capped
        if features_df['days_near_capacity'].max() >= max_reasonable_days:
            print(f"  ⚠️  Note: days_near_capacity capped at {max_reasonable_days} days (some values exceeded this)")

        print(f"  ✓ Capacity constraint features created:")
        print(f"    - Capacity indicators: near_capacity, at_capacity, over_capacity")
        print(f"    - Capacity zones: {features_df['capacity_zone'].value_counts().to_dict()}")
        print(f"    - Days near capacity (max): {features_df['days_near_capacity'].max()}")
        print(f"    - Days at capacity (max): {features_df['days_at_capacity'].max()}")
        print(f"    - Capacity statistics:")
        print(f"      Mean occupancy: {features_df['bed_occupancy_rate'].mean():.2%}")
        print(f"      Max occupancy: {features_df['bed_occupancy_rate'].max():.2%}")
        print(f"      % days near capacity: {(features_df['near_capacity'].sum() / len(features_df)) * 100:.1f}%")
        print(f"      % days at capacity: {(features_df['at_capacity'].sum() / len(features_df)) * 100:.1f}%")
    else:
        print("  ⚠️  bed_occupancy_rate not found in KPI data - skipping capacity features")

    if 'discharges' in kpi_data.columns:
        features_df['discharges'] = kpi_data['discharges']
        features_df['discharges_lag_1'] = features_df['discharges'].shift(1)
        features_df['discharges_lag_7'] = features_df['discharges'].shift(1)
    # Note: bed_occupancy_rate and bed_occupancy_lag_1 are already added in capacity constraint features above
    # Only add if not already present (for backwards compatibility)
    if 'bed_occupancy_rate' not in features_df.columns:
        if 'bed_occupancy' in kpi_data.columns or 'occupancy_rate' in kpi_data.columns:
            occ_col = 'bed_occupancy' if 'bed_occupancy' in kpi_data.columns else 'occupancy_rate'
            features_df['bed_occupancy_rate'] = kpi_data[occ_col]
            features_df['bed_occupancy_lag_1'] = features_df['bed_occupancy_rate'].shift(1)
    if 'avg_length_of_stay' in kpi_data.columns or 'avg_los' in kpi_data.columns:
        los_col = 'avg_length_of_stay' if 'avg_length_of_stay' in kpi_data.columns else 'avg_los'
        features_df['avg_length_of_stay'] = kpi_data[los_col]

    # ============================================================
    # CREATE LAGGED KPI FEATURES (to avoid data leakage)
    # ============================================================
    # KPI features for prediction models should be lagged to avoid using
    # current-period KPI values that may not be available at prediction time
    print("\n  Creating lagged KPI features...")

    # COVID patient percentage (Granger-causes bed_occupancy)
    if 'covid_patient_pct' in kpi_data.columns:
        features_df['covid_patient_pct'] = kpi_data['covid_patient_pct']
        features_df['covid_patient_pct_lag1'] = kpi_data['covid_patient_pct'].shift(1)
        features_df['covid_patient_pct_lag4'] = kpi_data['covid_patient_pct'].shift(4)
        print(f"    ✓ covid_patient_pct_lag1, covid_patient_pct_lag4 created")

    # ICU occupancy rate
    if 'icu_occupancy_rate' in kpi_data.columns:
        features_df['icu_occupancy_rate'] = kpi_data['icu_occupancy_rate']
        features_df['icu_occupancy_rate_lag1'] = kpi_data['icu_occupancy_rate'].shift(1)
        features_df['icu_occupancy_rate_lag4'] = kpi_data['icu_occupancy_rate'].shift(4)
        print(f"    ✓ icu_occupancy_rate_lag1, icu_occupancy_rate_lag4 created")

    print("✓ KPI features added (including lagged versions)")
else:
    print("⚠️  KPI data not available - skipping KPI features")
