# ============================================================
# ADVANCED FEATURE ENGINEERING
# ============================================================
# Additional features that can improve forecasting performance

if len(features_df) > 0:
    print("Creating advanced features...")

    # ============================================================
    # 1. EXPONENTIAL MOVING AVERAGES (EMA)
    # ============================================================
    # REMOVED: EMA features (redundant with rolling mean)
    # EMA and rolling mean are highly correlated (>0.90) and serve similar purposes
    # Rolling mean is more interpretable, standard, and less sensitive to noise
    # Recommendation: Use rolling_mean instead of EMA
    print("\n1. Exponential Moving Averages...")
    print("  ⚠️  EMA features REMOVED (redundant with rolling mean):")
    print("     - ema_7, ema_30, ema_change_7 removed")
    print("     - Use rolling_mean_4/30 instead (more interpretable, standard)")

    # ============================================================
    # 2. PERCENTILE-BASED ROLLING FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # Percentiles are more robust to outliers than means
    print("\n2. Percentile-based rolling features...")

    # Rolling percentiles (25th, 75th, 90th)
    # FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage
    lagged_occupancy = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)
    features_df['rolling_p25_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).quantile(0.25)
    features_df['rolling_p75_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).quantile(0.75)
    features_df['rolling_p90_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).quantile(0.90)

    features_df['rolling_p25_13'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).quantile(0.25)
    features_df['rolling_p75_13'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).quantile(0.75)

    print("  ✓ Percentile features created (p25, p75, p90 for 7-day and 30-day windows)")

    # ============================================================
    # 3. VOLATILITY AND VARIABILITY FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # Measure of how variable bed occupancy is
    # FIXED: Use correct window sizes for weekly data (4w, 13w)
    print("\n3. Volatility and variability features...")

    # Coefficient of Variation (CV) = std / mean
    # Higher CV = more variable/unpredictable
    # FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage
    lagged_occupancy = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)

    # 4-week window (approximately 1 month)
    rolling_mean_4 = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).mean()
    rolling_std_4 = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).std()
    features_df['cv_4w'] = rolling_std_4 / (rolling_mean_4 + 1e-6)  # Add small epsilon to avoid division by zero

    # 13-week window (approximately 1 quarter)
    if len(features_df) > 13:
        rolling_mean_13 = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).mean()
        rolling_std_13 = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).std()
        features_df['cv_13w'] = rolling_std_13 / (rolling_mean_13 + 1e-6)

    # Range (max - min) as a measure of variability
    # FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage
    features_df['rolling_range_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).max() - lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).min()
    if len(features_df) > 13:
        features_df['rolling_range_13'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).max() - lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).min()

    # Additional rolling aggregations: Skewness and Kurtosis
    # Skewness: measures asymmetry in distribution (positive = right-skewed, negative = left-skewed)
    # Kurtosis: measures tail heaviness (positive = heavy tails/extreme values, negative = light tails)
    from scipy.stats import skew, kurtosis

    # FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage
    lagged_occupancy = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)

    # FIXED: Use correct length checks matching window sizes
    features_df['rolling_skew_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).apply(
        lambda x: skew(x) if len(x) == 4 and x.std() > 0 else 0, raw=True
    )
    if len(features_df) > 13:
        features_df['rolling_skew_13'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).apply(
            lambda x: skew(x) if len(x) == 13 and x.std() > 0 else 0, raw=True
        )

    features_df['rolling_kurtosis_4'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).apply(
        lambda x: kurtosis(x) if len(x) == 4 and x.std() > 0 else 0, raw=True
    )
    if len(features_df) > 13:
        features_df['rolling_kurtosis_13'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).apply(
            lambda x: kurtosis(x) if len(x) == 13 and x.std() > 0 else 0, raw=True
        )

    # Fill NaN values
    volatility_cols = ['rolling_skew_4', 'rolling_kurtosis_4']
    if len(features_df) > 13:
        volatility_cols.extend(['rolling_skew_13', 'rolling_kurtosis_13'])
    for col in volatility_cols:
        if col in features_df.columns:
            features_df[col] = features_df[col].fillna(0)

    print("  ✓ Volatility features created (coefficient of variation, rolling range, skewness, kurtosis)")

    # ============================================================
    # 4. MOMENTUM AND ACCELERATION FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # REMOVED: Acceleration and momentum features (redundant or too noisy)
    # - Acceleration (second derivative) is too noisy and amplifies noise
    # - Momentum (rolling mean of changes) is redundant with change features
    # - Change features (bed_occupancy_change_1, bed_occupancy_change_1) already capture momentum
    print("\n4. Momentum and acceleration features...")
    print("  ⚠️  Acceleration/momentum features REMOVED:")
    print("     - bed_occupancy_acceleration, bed_occupancy_acceleration_7 (too noisy)")
    print("     - momentum_7, momentum_30 (redundant with change features)")
    print("     - Use bed_occupancy_change_1/7 instead (capture momentum directly)")

    # ============================================================
    # 5. TARGET ENCODING (MEAN ENCODING)
    # ============================================================
    # REMOVED: Target encoding features (DATA LEAKAGE - uses target variable to create features)
    # Target encoding can cause overfitting and data leakage if not done with proper time series cross-validation
    # Additionally, day-of-week and monthly effects are too weak (per EDA) to justify target encoding
    print("\n5. Target encoding (mean bed occupancy by category)...")
    print("  ⚠️  Target encoding features REMOVED (data leakage risk)")
    print("     - dow_mean_encoded, month_mean_encoded, weekend_mean_encoded removed")
    print("     - Day-of-week and monthly effects too weak per EDA")

    # ============================================================
    # 6. RATIO AND INTERACTION FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # REMOVED: Ratio features with current bed occupancy (DATA LEAKAGE - uses target variable)
    # Ratios that use current week's bed occupancy create data leakage
    print("\n6. Ratio and interaction features...")
    print("  ⚠️  Ratio features with current bed occupancy REMOVED (data leakage):")
    print("     - bed_occupancy_to_mean_7/30 (uses current bed occupancy)")
    print("     - bed_occupancy_to_discharges (uses current bed occupancy)")
    print("     - bed_occupancy_to_capacity (uses current bed occupancy)")
    print("  ✅ KEPT: bed_occupancy_lag1_to_discharges_lag1 (uses lagged values only, safe)")

    # Only keep ratio features that don't use current bed occupancy
    if 'discharges' in features_df.columns:
        # FIXED: Use lagged bed_occupancy to avoid data leakage (was using current bed_occupancy)
        # Lagged bed occupancy to lagged discharges ratio (safe - uses only past values)
        features_df['bed_occupancy_lag1_to_discharges_lag1'] = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1) / (features_df['discharges'].shift(1) + 1e-6)
        print("  ✓ Kept: bed_occupancy_lag1_to_discharges_lag1 (safe - uses lagged values only)")

    # ============================================================
    # 7. CALENDAR EFFECTS
    # ============================================================
    # Additional calendar-based features
    print("\n7. Calendar effects...")

    # First/last week of month (often have different patterns)
    features_df['is_first_week_of_month'] = (features_df.index.day <= 7).astype(int)
    features_df['is_last_week_of_month'] = (features_df.index.day >= (features_df.index.to_series().apply(lambda x: (x + pd.offsets.MonthEnd(0)).day) - 6)).astype(int)

    # Day of quarter (1-90/91/92)
    features_df['day_of_quarter'] = ((features_df.index.month - 1) % 3) * 30 + features_df.index.day

    # Week of quarter (1-13)
    quarter_start = features_df.index.to_series().apply(lambda x: pd.Timestamp(year=x.year, month=((x.month-1)//3)*3+1, day=1))
    features_df['week_of_quarter'] = ((features_df.index - quarter_start).dt.days // 7) + 1

    print("  ✓ Calendar effect features created (first/last week of month, day/week of quarter)")

    # ============================================================
    # 8. FOURIER FEATURES (ADDITIONAL FREQUENCY COMPONENTS)
    # ============================================================
    # Additional frequency components for complex seasonality
    print("\n8. Fourier features (additional frequency components)...")

    # REMOVED: Day-of-week and monthly harmonics (patterns too weak per EDA)
    # KEPT: Annual harmonics (annual seasonality is important)

    # Annual seasonality: second harmonic (period = 6 months)
    # This captures complex annual patterns beyond the first harmonic
    # Use dayofyear directly (day_of_year feature removed - less meaningful for weekly data)
    day_of_year_values = features_df.index.dayofyear  # Calculate but don't store as feature
    features_df['doy_harmonic2_sin'] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * day_of_year_values / 182.5)
    features_df['doy_harmonic2_cos'] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * day_of_year_values / 182.5)

    print("  ✓ Fourier harmonic features created:")
    print("     - Removed: dow_harmonic2, month_harmonic2 (patterns too weak per EDA)")
    print("     - Kept: doy_harmonic2 (annual harmonics - important)")

    # ============================================================
    # 9. AUTOCORRELATION FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # Lagged autocorrelations (how similar is current week to N weeks ago)
    # FIXED: Use appropriate window for weekly data (4 weeks)
    print("\n9. Autocorrelation features...")

    # Calculate rolling autocorrelation (correlation between current and lagged values)
    # This is computationally expensive, so we'll use a simpler approximation
    # For weekly data, use 4-week and 8-week windows
    # FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage
    lagged_occupancy = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)
    features_df['autocorr_lag4w_approx'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=8).apply(
        lambda x: x.iloc[-4:].corr(x.iloc[:4]) if len(x) == 8 and x.iloc[:4].std() > 0 else 0,
        raw=False
    )

    print("  ✓ Autocorrelation features created (approximate rolling autocorrelation)")

    # ============================================================
    # 10. TREND FEATURES
    # ============================================================
    # Linear trend components
    # FIXED: Use appropriate windows for weekly data (4w, 13w)
    print("\n10. Trend features...")

    # Weeks since start (linear trend)
    features_df['days_since_start'] = (features_df.index - features_df.index.min()).days

    # Rolling linear trend (slope of occupancy over rolling window)
    def rolling_trend(x):
        if len(x) < 2:
            return 0
        y = np.arange(len(x))
        slope = np.polyfit(y, x, 1)[0] if len(x) > 1 and np.std(x) > 0 else 0
        return slope

    # FIXED: Use lagged values to avoid data leakage
    lagged_occupancy = features_df['bed_occupancy'].shift(1)

    # 4-week trend (approximately 1 month)
    features_df['trend_4w'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=4).apply(rolling_trend, raw=True)
    # 13-week trend (approximately 1 quarter)
    if len(features_df) > 13:
        features_df['trend_13w'] = lagged_occupancy.rolling(window=13).apply(rolling_trend, raw=True)

    print("  ✓ Trend features created (days since start, rolling linear trend)")

        # Fill NaN values ONLY from features created in THIS cell (advanced features)
    # DO NOT fill NaN from lag/rolling features - those should be removed in cleaning step
    # UPDATED: Use new feature names for weekly data (4w, 13w, 52w instead of 7, 30, 365)
    advanced_feature_names = [
        # Removed: 'ema_7', 'ema_30', 'ema_change_7' (redundant with rolling mean)
        'rolling_p25_4', 'rolling_p75_4', 'rolling_p90_4', 'rolling_p25_13', 'rolling_p75_13',
        'cv_4w', 'cv_13w', 'rolling_range_4', 'rolling_range_13',
        # Removed: 'bed_occupancy_acceleration', 'bed_occupancy_acceleration_7' (too noisy)
        # Removed: 'momentum_7', 'momentum_30' (redundant with change features)
        # Removed: 'dow_mean_encoded', 'month_mean_encoded', 'weekend_mean_encoded' (data leakage)
        # Zero-inflation features (added to handle zero-inflated distribution)
        # UPDATED: Use weekly window names (4w, 13w, 52w)
        'was_zero_yesterday', 'was_zero_last_week', 'was_zero_last_year',
        'consecutive_zeros', 'prob_zero_4w', 'prob_zero_13w', 'prob_zero_52w',
        'days_since_nonzero', 'zeros_count_4w', 'zeros_count_13w',
        'was_extreme_high_yesterday', 'was_extreme_high_last_week', 'days_since_extreme_high',
        # Removed: 'bed_occupancy_to_mean_7', 'bed_occupancy_to_mean_30', 'bed_occupancy_to_discharges', 'bed_occupancy_to_capacity' (data leakage)
        'bed_occupancy_to_discharges_lag1',  # Safe - uses lagged discharges
        'is_first_week_of_month', 'is_last_week_of_month', 'day_of_quarter', 'week_of_quarter',
        # Removed: 'dow_harmonic2_sin', 'dow_harmonic2_cos', 'month_harmonic2_sin', 'month_harmonic2_cos' (weak patterns)
        'doy_harmonic2_sin', 'doy_harmonic2_cos',
        'autocorr_lag4w_approx',
        'days_since_start', 'trend_4w', 'trend_13w'
    ]

    # Only fill NaN for advanced features created in this cell
    advanced_feature_cols = [col for col in advanced_feature_names if col in features_df.columns]
    for col in advanced_feature_cols:
        if features_df[col].isna().any():
            # Fill with 0 for most features, or forward fill for trend features
            if 'trend' in col or 'autocorr' in col:
                features_df[col] = features_df[col].ffill().fillna(0)
            else:
                features_df[col] = features_df[col].fillna(0)

    print(f"\n✓ Advanced features created: {len(advanced_feature_cols)} new features")
    print(f"  Total features in dataset: {len([col for col in features_df.columns if col not in weekly_occupancy.columns])}")

else:
    print("⚠️  No data available for advanced feature engineering")

Feature Selection and Cleaning¶

In [ ]:
# Remove rows with NaN (from lag/rolling features at the beginning)
# This removes the first ~30 rows that have NaN from lag_30 and rolling features
# This is expected - we can't use those rows for modeling anyway (no historical data)

# ============================================================
# CONFIGURATION: Feature Selection Parameters
# ============================================================
# Model type determines correlation threshold (stricter for linear models)
INTENDED_MODEL_TYPE = 'tree'  # Options: 'linear', 'tree', 'neural'
CORRELATION_THRESHOLDS = {
    'linear': 0.90,      # Stricter for linear models (more aggressive)
    'tree': 0.98,        # More lenient for tree models (handle multicollinearity well)
    'neural': 0.95,      # Moderate for neural networks
}
CORRELATION_THRESHOLD = CORRELATION_THRESHOLDS.get(INTENDED_MODEL_TYPE, 0.95)
MAX_CORRELATION_ITERATIONS = 3  # Iteratively reduce correlations
VIF_THRESHOLD = 10
IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD = 0.3  # For VIF hybrid approach
MIN_IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD = 0.08  # Optional: remove very low importance features
USE_MUTUAL_INFORMATION = True  # Calculate mutual information
EXPORT_REPORT = True  # Export feature selection report

if len(features_df) > 0 and len(train_data) > 0 and len(test_data) > 0:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("FEATURE SELECTION (TRAIN/TEST SPLIT AWARE)")
    print("="*60)
    print("⚠️  CRITICAL: Performing feature selection on TRAINING DATA ONLY")
    print("   This prevents data leakage from test set into feature selection")
    print(f"   Model type: {INTENDED_MODEL_TYPE} (correlation threshold: {CORRELATION_THRESHOLD})")

    # Step 0: Prepare full feature frame (keep NaNs for now)
    # We will handle NaNs separately in each step (e.g., VIF, MI) to avoid
    # accidentally removing all test rows before splitting.
    features_df_clean_full = features_df.copy()

    # Split into train and test BEFORE feature selection
    # Use intersection to handle potential index mismatches gracefully
    train_indices = features_df_clean_full.index.intersection(train_data.index)
    test_indices = features_df_clean_full.index.intersection(test_data.index)

    if len(train_indices) == 0:
        print("⚠️  WARNING: No matching indices between features_df and train_data!")
        print("   This may indicate a data alignment issue.")
        # Keep same columns as features_df_clean_full but with no rows
        train_features_raw = features_df_clean_full.loc[train_indices].copy()
    else:
        train_features_raw = features_df_clean_full.loc[train_indices].copy()

    if len(test_indices) == 0:
        print("⚠️  WARNING: No matching indices between features_df and test_data!")
        print("   This may indicate a data alignment issue.")
        # Keep same columns as features_df_clean_full but with no rows
        test_features_raw = features_df_clean_full.loc[test_indices].copy()
    else:
        test_features_raw = features_df_clean_full.loc[test_indices].copy()

    # FIXED: Filter for NUMERIC columns only (exclude strings, dates, objects)
    # This prevents errors when computing std() for feature selection
    # Also drop EXCLUDE_FEATURES (redundant or not significant per EDA)
    exclude_cols = ['bed_occupancy', 'week_of_year_name', 'month_name']
    numeric_dtypes = ['int64', 'int32', 'float64', 'float32', 'int', 'float']
    initial_feature_cols = [
        col for col in features_df_clean_full.columns
        if col not in exclude_cols
        and col not in EXCLUDE_FEATURES
        and features_df_clean_full[col].dtype.name in numeric_dtypes
    ]

    # Report any non-numeric columns that were excluded
    non_numeric_cols = [col for col in features_df_clean_full.columns
                        if col not in exclude_cols
                        and col != 'bed_occupancy'
                        and features_df_clean_full[col].dtype.name not in numeric_dtypes]
    if non_numeric_cols:
        print(f"ℹ️  Excluded {len(non_numeric_cols)} non-numeric columns: {non_numeric_cols}")

    print(f"\nInitial dataset: {len(features_df_clean_full)} rows | {len(initial_feature_cols)} features")
    print(f"Train set: {len(train_features_raw)} rows")
    print(f"Test set: {len(test_features_raw)} rows")

    # Initialize feature selection tracking
    all_removed_features = []
    feature_cols = initial_feature_cols.copy()
    train_features = train_features_raw.copy()
    test_features = test_features_raw.copy()

    # ============================================================
    # STEP 1: CONSTANT FEATURE REMOVAL (on training data only)
    # ============================================================
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("STEP 1: Constant Feature Removal")
    print("="*60)

    constant_features = []
    for col in feature_cols:
        if train_features[col].nunique() <= 1 or train_features[col].std() == 0:
            constant_features.append(col)

    if constant_features:
        print(f"⚠️  Found {len(constant_features)} constant features (will be removed):")
        for feat in sorted(constant_features):
            print(f"   - {feat}")
        feature_cols = [col for col in feature_cols if col not in constant_features]
        train_features = train_features.drop(columns=constant_features)
        test_features = test_features.drop(columns=constant_features)
        all_removed_features.extend(constant_features)
        print(f"✓ Removed {len(constant_features)} constant features")
        print(f"  Remaining features: {len(feature_cols)}")
    else:
        print("✓ No constant features found")

    # ============================================================
    # STEP 2: FEATURE IMPORTANCE (correlation and mutual information)
    # ============================================================
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("STEP 2: Feature Importance Analysis")
    print("="*60)

    # Calculate correlation-based importance (on training data only)
    feature_importance_dict = {}
    if 'bed_occupancy' in train_features.columns and len(train_features) > 0:
        for col in feature_cols:
            if col != 'bed_occupancy' and col in train_features.columns:
                try:
                    corr = train_features[col].corr(train_features['bed_occupancy'])
                    if not np.isnan(corr):
                        feature_importance_dict[col] = abs(corr)
                except:
                    pass
    else:
        print("⚠️  WARNING: 'bed_occupancy' column not found in train_features - skipping correlation-based importance")

    # Calculate mutual information (non-linear relationships)
    feature_mi_dict = {}
    if USE_MUTUAL_INFORMATION and len(feature_cols) > 0:
        try:
            from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_regression
            # Drop rows with NaNs only for MI calculation
            X_train_mi = train_features[feature_cols].replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna()
            y_train_mi = train_features.loc[X_train_mi.index, 'bed_occupancy']
            if len(X_train_mi) > 0:
                mi_scores = mutual_info_regression(X_train_mi, y_train_mi, random_state=42)
                feature_mi_dict = dict(zip(feature_cols, mi_scores))
                print("✓ Mutual information calculated (captures non-linear relationships)")
            else:
                print("⚠️  Not enough non-NaN rows to calculate mutual information")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠️  Could not calculate mutual information: {e}")

    # Display top features
    feature_importance_sorted = sorted(feature_importance_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    print(f"\n📊 Top 10 Features by Correlation with Bed Occupancy:")
    for i, (feat, imp) in enumerate(feature_importance_sorted[:10], 1):
        print(f"  {i:2d}. {feat:30s} | Correlation: {imp:.4f}")

    if feature_mi_dict:
        feature_mi_sorted = sorted(feature_mi_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        print(f"\n📊 Top 10 Features by Mutual Information:")
        for i, (feat, mi) in enumerate(feature_mi_sorted[:10], 1):
            print(f"  {i:2d}. {feat:30s} | MI: {mi:.4f}")

    # ============================================================
    # STEP 3: CORRELATION-BASED MULTICOLLINEARITY REMOVAL
    # ============================================================
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print(f"STEP 3: Correlation-Based Removal (threshold: {CORRELATION_THRESHOLD})")
    print("="*60)

    # Priority list for keeping features
    # UPDATED: Added cyclical features (sin/cos) to priority list - important for linear models and neural networks
    # Cyclical encoding features are better than raw numeric dates for capturing cyclical patterns
    # FIXED: Removed duplicate entries, updated feature names for weekly data
    keep_priority = [
        'quarter', 'week_of_month', 'year',  # day_of_year removed (raw value, keep sin/cos only)
        # is_weekend removed - always 1 for weekly Sunday data (constant/useless)
        # Cyclical encoding features (added to priority list - important for linear/neural models)
        'day_of_year_sin', 'day_of_year_cos', 'quarter_sin', 'quarter_cos',
        # Lag features (based on ACF/PACF from EDA: lags 1, 3, 4, 52)
        'bed_occupancy_lag_1', 'bed_occupancy_lag_3', 'bed_occupancy_lag_4', 'bed_occupancy_lag_52',
        'discharges_lag_1',
        # Rolling statistics (4-week, 13-week, 52-week windows for weekly data)
        'rolling_mean_4', 'rolling_mean_13', 'rolling_mean_52',
        'rolling_std_4', 'rolling_min_4',
        # Capacity features
        'bed_occupancy_rate', 'near_capacity', 'capacity_zone', 'days_near_capacity',
        'discharges',
        # Zero-inflation features (updated names for weekly data)
        'was_zero_yesterday', 'consecutive_zeros', 'prob_zero_4w',
        'days_since_extreme_high',
        # External features (from EDA)
        'ili', 'flu_activity_level', 'temp_avg',
    ]

    print("📋 Priority list includes cyclical encoding features (day_of_year_sin/cos, quarter_sin/cos)")
    print("   These are important for linear models and neural networks to capture cyclical patterns")

    explicit_remove = [
        'days_since_start', 'month', 'week_of_month', 'quarter_doy_interaction',
    ]

    # Iterative correlation reduction
    correlation_features_removed = []
    for iteration in range(MAX_CORRELATION_ITERATIONS):
        if len(feature_cols) <= 1:
            break

        numeric_features = [col for col in feature_cols
                           if train_features[col].dtype in [np.float64, np.float32, np.int64, np.int32]]
        if len(numeric_features) <= 1:
            break

        # Calculate correlation matrix on training data only
        corr_matrix = train_features[numeric_features].corr().abs()

        # Find high correlation pairs
        high_corr_pairs = []
        for i in range(len(corr_matrix.columns)):
            for j in range(i+1, len(corr_matrix.columns)):
                if corr_matrix.iloc[i, j] > CORRELATION_THRESHOLD:
                    high_corr_pairs.append((
                        corr_matrix.columns[i],
                        corr_matrix.columns[j],
                        corr_matrix.iloc[i, j]
                    ))

        if not high_corr_pairs:
            if iteration == 0:
                print("✓ No highly correlated feature pairs found")
            else:
                print(f"✓ Iteration {iteration + 1}: No high correlations remaining")
            break

        if iteration == 0:
            print(f"⚠️  Found {len(high_corr_pairs)} highly correlated pairs (correlation > {CORRELATION_THRESHOLD})")
            if len(high_corr_pairs) <= 20:
                for feat1, feat2, corr_val in high_corr_pairs:
                    print(f"    {feat1:30s} <-> {feat2:30s} | r = {corr_val:.3f}")
            else:
                for feat1, feat2, corr_val in high_corr_pairs[:10]:
                    print(f"    {feat1:30s} <-> {feat2:30s} | r = {corr_val:.3f}")
                print(f"    ... and {len(high_corr_pairs) - 10} more pairs")

        # Determine which features to remove
        features_to_remove_iter = set()

        # Add explicit removals
        for feat in explicit_remove:
            if feat in feature_cols:
                features_to_remove_iter.add(feat)

        # Process each high correlation pair
        for feat1, feat2, corr_val in high_corr_pairs:
            if feat1 in features_to_remove_iter or feat2 in features_to_remove_iter:
                continue

            remove_feat = None

            # Rule 0: Perfect correlations
            if corr_val >= 0.999:
                if feat1 in keep_priority and feat2 not in keep_priority:
                    remove_feat = feat2
                elif feat2 in keep_priority and feat1 not in keep_priority:
                    remove_feat = feat1
                else:
                    remove_feat = feat2 if len(feat1) <= len(feat2) else feat1

            # Rule 1: Explicit removals
            elif feat1 in explicit_remove:
                remove_feat = feat1
            elif feat2 in explicit_remove:
                remove_feat = feat2

            # Rule 2: Priority list
            elif feat1 in keep_priority and feat2 not in keep_priority:
                remove_feat = feat2
            elif feat2 in keep_priority and feat1 not in keep_priority:
                remove_feat = feat1

            # Rule 3: Feature importance (use correlation or MI)
            else:
                imp1 = feature_importance_dict.get(feat1, 0)
                imp2 = feature_importance_dict.get(feat2, 0)
                if feature_mi_dict:
                    mi1 = feature_mi_dict.get(feat1, 0)
                    mi2 = feature_mi_dict.get(feat2, 0)
                    # Use average of correlation and MI
                    score1 = (imp1 + mi1) / 2
                    score2 = (imp2 + mi2) / 2
                    if score1 > score2:
                        remove_feat = feat2
                    elif score2 > score1:
                        remove_feat = feat1
                    else:
                        remove_feat = feat2 if len(feat1) > len(feat2) else feat1
                else:
                    if imp1 > imp2:
                        remove_feat = feat2
                    elif imp2 > imp1:
                        remove_feat = feat1
                    else:
                        remove_feat = feat2 if len(feat1) > len(feat2) else feat1

            if remove_feat and remove_feat in feature_cols and remove_feat not in keep_priority:
                features_to_remove_iter.add(remove_feat)

        if features_to_remove_iter:
            print(f"\n  Iteration {iteration + 1}: Removing {len(features_to_remove_iter)} redundant features")
            if len(features_to_remove_iter) <= 20:
                for feat in sorted(features_to_remove_iter):
                    print(f"    - {feat}")
            else:
                for feat in sorted(list(features_to_remove_iter))[:10]:
                    print(f"    - {feat}")
                print(f"    ... and {len(features_to_remove_iter) - 10} more")

            feature_cols = [col for col in feature_cols if col not in features_to_remove_iter]
            train_features = train_features.drop(columns=list(features_to_remove_iter))
            test_features = test_features.drop(columns=list(features_to_remove_iter))
            correlation_features_removed.extend(features_to_remove_iter)
            all_removed_features.extend(features_to_remove_iter)
            print(f"  ✓ Removed {len(features_to_remove_iter)} features | Remaining: {len(feature_cols)}")
        else:
            break

    # Check remaining high correlations
    remaining_high_corr = []
    if len(feature_cols) > 1:
        numeric_remaining = [col for col in feature_cols
                             if train_features[col].dtype in [np.float64, np.float32, np.int64, np.int32]]
        if len(numeric_remaining) > 1:
            corr_matrix_final = train_features[numeric_remaining].corr().abs()
            for i in range(len(corr_matrix_final.columns)):
                for j in range(i+1, len(corr_matrix_final.columns)):
                    if corr_matrix_final.iloc[i, j] > CORRELATION_THRESHOLD:
                        remaining_high_corr.append((
                            corr_matrix_final.columns[i],
                            corr_matrix_final.columns[j],
                            corr_matrix_final.iloc[i, j]
                        ))

            if remaining_high_corr:
                print(f"\n⚠️  Remaining Highly Correlated Pairs ({len(remaining_high_corr)}):")
                for feat1, feat2, corr_val in sorted(remaining_high_corr, key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)[:10]:
                    print(f"   - {feat1:25s} <-> {feat2:25s} | r = {corr_val:.3f}")
                if len(remaining_high_corr) > 10:
                    print(f"   ... and {len(remaining_high_corr) - 10} more pairs")
            else:
                print(f"\n✓ All highly correlated pairs removed!")

            # ============================================================
            # MANUAL RESOLUTION: near_capacity vs capacity_zone correlation
            # ============================================================
            # These two features have r=0.991 - both are in priority list, so manual resolution needed
            if 'near_capacity' in feature_cols and 'capacity_zone' in feature_cols:
                # Check correlation between them
                try:
                    corr_near_zone = train_features['near_capacity'].corr(train_features['capacity_zone'])
                    if abs(corr_near_zone) > 0.95:  # Very high correlation
                        print(f"\n🔧 Manual Resolution: near_capacity vs capacity_zone")
                        print(f"   Correlation: {corr_near_zone:.3f} (very high - >0.95)")

                        # Compare importance to decide which to keep

                        imp_zone = feature_importance_dict.get('capacity_zone', 0)

                        print(f"   near_capacity importance: {imp_near:.4f}")
                        print(f"   capacity_zone importance: {imp_zone:.4f}")

                        # Prefer capacity_zone (more interpretable categorical encoding)
                        # Both have similar importance, so choose the more interpretable one
                        if abs(imp_zone - imp_near) < 0.05:  # Similar importance (within 5%)
                            print(f"   Decision: Removing 'near_capacity' (capacity_zone is more interpretable)")
                            print(f"   Rationale: capacity_zone provides categorical encoding (Low/Medium/High/Critical)")
                            print(f"              which is more informative than binary near_capacity indicator")
                            if 'near_capacity' in feature_cols:
                                feature_cols.remove('near_capacity')
                                train_features = train_features.drop(columns=['near_capacity'])
                                test_features = test_features.drop(columns=['near_capacity'])
                                all_removed_features.append('near_capacity')
                                correlation_features_removed.append('near_capacity')
                                print(f"   ✓ Removed 'near_capacity' | Remaining features: {len(feature_cols)}")
                        else:
                            # Keep the more important one
                            if imp_zone > imp_near:
                                print(f"   Decision: Removing 'near_capacity' (capacity_zone has higher importance)")
                                if 'near_capacity' in feature_cols:
                                    feature_cols.remove('near_capacity')
                                    train_features = train_features.drop(columns=['near_capacity'])
                                    test_features = test_features.drop(columns=['near_capacity'])
                                    all_removed_features.append('near_capacity')
                                    correlation_features_removed.append('near_capacity')
                                    print(f"   ✓ Removed 'near_capacity' | Remaining features: {len(feature_cols)}")
                            else:
                                print(f"   Decision: Removing 'capacity_zone' (near_capacity has higher importance)")
                                if 'capacity_zone' in feature_cols:
                                    feature_cols.remove('capacity_zone')
                                    train_features = train_features.drop(columns=['capacity_zone'])
                                    test_features = test_features.drop(columns=['capacity_zone'])

                                    print(f"   ✓ Removed 'capacity_zone' | Remaining features: {len(feature_cols)}")
                except Exception as e:

            # ============================================================
            # MANUAL RESOLUTION: near_capacity vs capacity_zone correlation
            # ============================================================
            # These two features have r=0.991 - both are in priority list, so manual resolution needed
            if 'near_capacity' in feature_cols and 'capacity_zone' in feature_cols:
                # Check correlation between them
                try:
                    corr_near_zone = train_features['near_capacity'].corr(train_features['capacity_zone'])
                    if abs(corr_near_zone) > 0.95:  # Very high correlation
                        print(f"\n🔧 Manual Resolution: near_capacity vs capacity_zone")
                        print(f"   Correlation: {corr_near_zone:.3f} (very high - >0.95)")

                        # Compare importance to decide which to keep
                        imp_near = feature_importance_dict.get('near_capacity', 0)
                        imp_zone = feature_importance_dict.get('capacity_zone', 0)

                        print(f"   near_capacity importance: {imp_near:.4f}")
                        print(f"   capacity_zone importance: {imp_zone:.4f}")

                        # Prefer capacity_zone (more interpretable categorical encoding)
                        # Both have similar importance, so choose the more interpretable one
                        if abs(imp_zone - imp_near) < 0.05:  # Similar importance (within 5%)
                            print(f"   Decision: Removing 'near_capacity' (capacity_zone is more interpretable)")
                            print(f"   Rationale: capacity_zone provides categorical encoding (Low/Medium/High/Critical)")
                            print(f"              which is more informative than binary near_capacity indicator")
                            if 'near_capacity' in feature_cols:
                                feature_cols.remove('near_capacity')

                                all_removed_features.append('near_capacity')
                                correlation_features_removed.append('near_capacity')
                                print(f"   ✓ Removed 'near_capacity' | Remaining features: {len(feature_cols)}")
                        else:
                            # Keep the more important one
                            if imp_zone > imp_near:
                                print(f"   Decision: Removing 'near_capacity' (capacity_zone has higher importance)")
                                if 'near_capacity' in feature_cols:
                                    feature_cols.remove('near_capacity')
                                    train_features = train_features.drop(columns=['near_capacity'])

                                    correlation_features_removed.append('capacity_zone')
                                    print(f"   ✓ Removed 'capacity_zone' | Remaining features: {len(feature_cols)}")
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"   ⚠️  Could not resolve near_capacity vs capacity_zone correlation: {e}")

    # ============================================================
    # STEP 4: VIF FILTERING (Hybrid Approach)
    # ============================================================
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("STEP 4: VIF Filtering (Hybrid Approach)")
    print("="*60)
    print(f"  VIF Threshold: {VIF_THRESHOLD} | Importance Threshold: {IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD}")
    print("  Only removes features with high VIF AND low importance")

    vif_features_removed = []
    vif_scores = {}
    vif_keep_priority = keep_priority.copy()

    if len(feature_cols) > 1:
        numeric_for_vif = [col for col in feature_cols
                           if train_features[col].dtype in [np.float64, np.float32, np.int64, np.int32]
                           and col in train_features.columns]

        if len(numeric_for_vif) > 1:
            try:
                from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
                from sklearn.metrics import r2_score

                vif_data = train_features[numeric_for_vif].copy()
                vif_data = vif_data.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).dropna()

                if len(vif_data) > len(numeric_for_vif) + 1:
                    features_to_remove_vif = set()

                    for feature in numeric_for_vif:
                        try:
                            X = vif_data.drop(columns=[feature])
                            y = vif_data[feature]

                            reg = LinearRegression()
                            reg.fit(X, y)
                            r2 = r2_score(y, reg.predict(X))

                            if r2 >= 1.0 or np.isnan(r2):
                                vif = np.inf
                            elif r2 == 0:
                                vif = 1.0
                            else:
                                vif = 1 / (1 - r2)

                            vif_scores[feature] = vif

                            # Hybrid approach: remove only if high VIF AND low importance
                            importance = feature_importance_dict.get(feature, 0)
                            if vif > VIF_THRESHOLD and importance < IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD:
                                if feature not in vif_keep_priority:
                                    features_to_remove_vif.add(feature)
                        except Exception as e:
                            continue

                    # Report VIF results
                    high_vif_features = {f: vif for f, vif in vif_scores.items() if vif > VIF_THRESHOLD}
                    high_vif_high_imp = {f: (vif, feature_importance_dict.get(f, 0))
                                         for f, vif in high_vif_features.items()
                                         if feature_importance_dict.get(f, 0) >= IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD}
                    high_vif_low_imp = {f: (vif, feature_importance_dict.get(f, 0))
                                        for f, vif in high_vif_features.items()
                                        if feature_importance_dict.get(f, 0) < IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD
                                        and f not in vif_keep_priority}

                    if high_vif_features:
                        print(f"\n  Found {len(high_vif_features)} features with VIF > {VIF_THRESHOLD}:")
                        if high_vif_high_imp:
                            print(f"    ✓ Keeping {len(high_vif_high_imp)} with high importance (>= {IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD})")
                            for feat, (vif_val, imp) in sorted(high_vif_high_imp.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][0], reverse=True)[:5]:
                                print(f"      {feat:30s} | VIF: {vif_val:8.2f} | Importance: {imp:.4f}")

                        if high_vif_low_imp:
                            print(f"    ⚠️  Removing {len(high_vif_low_imp)} with high VIF AND low importance (< {IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD}):")
                            for feat, (vif_val, imp) in sorted(high_vif_low_imp.items(), key=lambda x: x[1][0], reverse=True):
                                print(f"      {feat:30s} | VIF: {vif_val:8.2f} | Importance: {imp:.4f}")

                    if features_to_remove_vif:
                        print(f"\n📋 Features Removed by VIF Filtering ({len(features_to_remove_vif)}):")
                        for feat in sorted(features_to_remove_vif):
                            vif_val = vif_scores.get(feat, 0)
                            importance = feature_importance_dict.get(feat, 0)
                            print(f"   - {feat:30s} | VIF: {vif_val:8.2f} | Importance: {importance:.4f}")

                        feature_cols = [col for col in feature_cols if col not in features_to_remove_vif]
                        train_features = train_features.drop(columns=list(features_to_remove_vif))
                        test_features = test_features.drop(columns=list(features_to_remove_vif))
                        vif_features_removed.extend(features_to_remove_vif)
                        all_removed_features.extend(features_to_remove_vif)
                        print(f"  ✓ Removed {len(features_to_remove_vif)} features | Remaining: {len(feature_cols)}")
                    else:
                        print("\n✓ No features removed by VIF filtering (all protected or have high importance)")
                else:
                    print(f"  ⚠️  Insufficient data for VIF (need more rows than features)")
            except ImportError:
                print("  ⚠️  sklearn not available - skipping VIF calculation")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ⚠️  Error calculating VIF: {e}")

    # ============================================================
    # STEP 5: OPTIONAL LOW IMPORTANCE REMOVAL
    # ============================================================
    low_importance_removed = []
    if MIN_IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD > 0:
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print(f"STEP 5: Low Importance Feature Removal (optional, threshold: {MIN_IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD})")
        print("="*60)

        low_importance_features = [
            feat for feat in feature_cols
            if feature_importance_dict.get(feat, 0) < MIN_IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD
            and feat not in keep_priority
        ]

        if low_importance_features:
            print(f"⚠️  Found {len(low_importance_features)} features with very low importance")
            for feat in sorted(low_importance_features):
                imp = feature_importance_dict.get(feat, 0)
                print(f"   - {feat:30s} | Importance: {imp:.4f}")
            print("  Note: Not removing by default (can uncomment to enable)")

            # train_features = train_features.drop(columns=low_importance_features)
            # test_features = test_features.drop(columns=low_importance_features)
            # low_importance_removed.extend(low_importance_features)
            # all_removed_features.extend(low_importance_features)
        else:
            print("✓ No features with very low importance found")

    # ============================================================
    # STEP 6: FINAL SUMMARY AND REPORT
    # ============================================================
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("FEATURE SELECTION SUMMARY")
    print("="*60)

    features_df_clean = pd.concat([train_features, test_features]).sort_index()

    print(f"  Initial features: {len(initial_feature_cols)}")
    print(f"  Removed constant: {len(constant_features)}")
    print(f"  Removed correlation: {len(correlation_features_removed)}")
    print(f"  Removed VIF: {len(vif_features_removed)}")
    print(f"  Removed low importance: {len(low_importance_removed)}")
    print(f"  Final features: {len(feature_cols)}")
    print(f"  Total removed: {len(all_removed_features)} ({len(all_removed_features)/len(initial_feature_cols)*100:.1f}%)")

    print(f"\nFinal Dataset:")
    print(f"  Train: {len(train_features)} rows × {len(feature_cols)} features")
    print(f"  Test: {len(test_features)} rows × {len(feature_cols)} features")
    print(f"  Total: {len(features_df_clean)} rows × {len(feature_cols)} features")

    # ============================================================
    # FEATURE CATEGORIZATION AND SUMMARY
    # ============================================================
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("📊 FINAL FEATURE SET BY CATEGORY")
    print("="*60)

    # Categorize final features
    feature_categories = {
        'Temporal': [f for f in feature_cols if any(x in f for x in ['quarter', 'day_of_year', 'week_of_month', 'week_of_year', 'month', 'year', 'week_of_', 'is_month_', 'is_quarter_'])],
        'Cyclical Encoding': [f for f in feature_cols if '_sin' in f or '_cos' in f],
        'Holiday/Weekend': [f for f in feature_cols if any(x in f for x in ['holiday', 'weekend'])],
        'Lag Features': [f for f in feature_cols if 'lag' in f],
        'Lag-Temporal Interactions': [f for f in feature_cols if ('lag' in f and ('weekend' in f or 'holiday' in f or 'quarter' in f))],
        'Rolling Statistics': [f for f in feature_cols if 'rolling_' in f],
        'Change Features': [f for f in feature_cols if 'change' in f or 'pct_change' in f],
        'Capacity': [f for f in feature_cols if 'capacity' in f or 'occupancy' in f],
        'KPI': [f for f in feature_cols if any(x in f for x in ['discharges', 'length_of_stay', 'los'])],
        'Volatility': [f for f in feature_cols if any(x in f for x in ['cv_', 'rolling_range', 'rolling_std'])],
        'Percentile': [f for f in feature_cols if 'p25' in f or 'p75' in f or 'p90' in f],
        'Trend': [f for f in feature_cols if 'trend' in f or 'days_since_start' in f],
        'Fourier/Harmonic': [f for f in feature_cols if 'harmonic' in f or 'doy_harmonic' in f],
        'Calendar Effects': [f for f in feature_cols if any(x in f for x in ['first_week', 'last_week', 'day_of_quarter', 'week_of_quarter'])],
        'Time-Based': [f for f in feature_cols if 'days_since' in f or 'days_at' in f or 'days_near' in f],
        'Other': []
    }

    # Find uncategorized features
    categorized_features = set()
    for category, features in feature_categories.items():
        categorized_features.update(features)
    feature_categories['Other'] = [f for f in feature_cols if f not in categorized_features]

    # Print categorized summary
    for category, features in feature_categories.items():
        if features:
            print(f"\n  {category} ({len(features)} features):")
            # Group features by importance (if available)
            if feature_importance_dict:
                features_with_imp = [(f, feature_importance_dict.get(f, 0)) for f in features]
                features_with_imp.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
                for feat, imp in features_with_imp[:10]:  # Show top 10 per category
                    print(f"    - {feat:35s} (importance: {imp:.4f})")
                if len(features_with_imp) > 10:
                    print(f"    ... and {len(features_with_imp) - 10} more")
            else:
                for feat in sorted(features)[:10]:
                    print(f"    - {feat}")
                if len(features) > 10:
                    print(f"    ... and {len(features) - 10} more")

    # Summary statistics by category
    print(f"\n📈 Feature Category Statistics:")
    total_categorized = sum(len(features) for category, features in feature_categories.items() if category != 'Other')
    print(f"  Total categorized features: {total_categorized}/{len(feature_cols)}")
    if feature_categories['Other']:
        print(f"  Uncategorized (Other): {len(feature_categories['Other'])}")
        print(f"    Features: {', '.join(feature_categories['Other'][:5])}")
        if len(feature_categories['Other']) > 5:
            print(f"    ... and {len(feature_categories['Other']) - 5} more")

    # Store categories for export
    feature_categories_export = {k: v for k, v in feature_categories.items() if v}

    # Export feature selection report
    if EXPORT_REPORT:

            'initial_features': initial_feature_cols,

            'model_type': INTENDED_MODEL_TYPE,
            'correlation_threshold': CORRELATION_THRESHOLD,
            'feature_categories': feature_categories_export if 'feature_categories_export' in locals() else {},
        }

        import json
        report_file = os.path.join(DATA_PROCESSED, 'feature_selection_report.json')
        with open(report_file, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(feature_selection_report, f, indent=2)
        print(f"\n✓ Feature selection report saved: {report_file}")

        if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED:

            with open(report_file_drive, 'w') as f:
                json.dump(feature_selection_report, f, indent=2)
            print(f"✓ Feature selection report saved to Google Drive")

    print("\n✓ Feature selection complete!")

Create Model-Specific Feature Sets¶

Create pre-configured feature sets optimized for different model types. This makes it easier for models in notebook 04 to load and use features without selection logic.

In [ ]:
# Create model-specific feature sets for easy loading in notebook 04
if len(features_df_clean) > 0:
    print("Creating model-specific feature sets...")

    # Feature sets for different model types
    feature_sets = {}

    # 1. ARIMAX/SARIMAX: Exogenous variables (temporal + external features, no lags)
    #    Uses centralized ARIMAX_FEATURES config (single source of truth)
    arimax_features = []
    # Cyclical encoding for seasonality
    for feat in ARIMAX_FEATURES.get('cyclical', []):
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns and feat not in arimax_features:
            arimax_features.append(feat)
    # External + calendar features
    for feat in ARIMAX_FEATURES.get('exogenous', []):
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns and feat not in arimax_features:
            arimax_features.append(feat)
    # KPI lags (e.g., covid_patient_pct_lag1)
    for feat in ARIMAX_FEATURES.get('kpi_lagged', []):
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns and feat not in arimax_features:
            arimax_features.append(feat)
    feature_sets['arimax_exog'] = arimax_features
    print(f"  ✓ ARIMAX/SARIMAX features ({len(arimax_features)}): {arimax_features}")

    # 2. LSTM: All relevant features (temporal, lag, rolling stats, KPIs, external, cyclical encoding)
    #    Uses centralized LSTM_FEATURES + SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES for externals
    lstm_features = []
    # Cyclical encoding (better for neural networks)
    for feat in ['quarter_sin', 'quarter_cos', 'day_of_year_sin', 'day_of_year_cos']:
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns:
            lstm_features.append(feat)
    # REMOVED: Temporal flags (is_weekend always 1, is_holiday removed - not useful for weekly data)
    # Lag features (updated based on ACF/PACF analysis: lags 1, 3, 4, 52)
    for feat in ['bed_occupancy_lag_1', 'bed_occupancy_lag_3', 'bed_occupancy_lag_4', 'bed_occupancy_lag_52']:
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns:
            lstm_features.append(feat)
    # Rolling statistics
    for feat in ['rolling_mean_4', 'rolling_median_4', 'rolling_std_4']:
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns:
            lstm_features.append(feat)
    # Change features (momentum)
    for feat in ['bed_occupancy_change_1', 'bed_occupancy_pct_change_1']:
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns:
            lstm_features.append(feat)
    # External features - USE LAGGED VERSIONS ONLY to avoid data leakage
    # (Non-lagged ili/temp_min may not be available at prediction time due to reporting lag)
    # FIXED: Removed non-lagged SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES to prevent leakage
    for base_feat in SELECTED_EXTERNAL_FEATURES:
        for lag in [1, 4]:
            feat = f"{base_feat}_lag_{lag}"
            if feat in features_df_clean.columns:
                lstm_features.append(feat)
    # Differenced features (for stationarity)
    for feat in ['bed_occupancy_diff_1', 'bed_occupancy_diff_52']:
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns:
            lstm_features.append(feat)
    # KPI features (if available)
    for feat in ['discharges_lag_1', 'bed_occupancy_lag_1']:
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns:
            lstm_features.append(feat)
    feature_sets['lstm'] = lstm_features
    print(f"  ✓ LSTM features ({len(lstm_features)}): {lstm_features[:10]}... (+{len(lstm_features)-10} more)" if len(lstm_features) > 10 else f"  ✓ LSTM features ({len(lstm_features)}): {lstm_features}")

    # 3. VAR: Temporal features + external as exogenous (VAR already uses multiple KPIs)
    #    Uses centralized VAR_FEATURES config for exogenous variables
    var_exog_features = []
    # Cyclical encoding
    for feat in ['quarter_sin', 'quarter_cos', 'day_of_year_sin', 'day_of_year_cos']:
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns:
            var_exog_features.append(feat)
    # REMOVED: Temporal flags (is_weekend always 1, is_holiday removed - not useful for weekly data)
    # External features (from centralized VAR_FEATURES['exogenous'])
    for feat in VAR_FEATURES.get('exogenous', []):
        if feat in features_df_clean.columns and feat not in var_exog_features:
            var_exog_features.append(feat)
    feature_sets['var_exog'] = var_exog_features
    print(f"  ✓ VAR exogenous features ({len(var_exog_features)}): {var_exog_features}")

    # Save feature sets as separate CSV files for easy loading
    print("\nSaving model-specific feature sets...")

    # Save ARIMAX/SARIMAX features
    if len(arimax_features) > 0:
        arimax_df = features_df_clean[['bed_occupancy'] + arimax_features].copy()
        arimax_file_local = os.path.join(DATA_PROCESSED, 'features_for_arimax.csv')
        arimax_df.to_csv(arimax_file_local)
        print(f"  ✓ Saved to local: {arimax_file_local} | Shape: {arimax_df.shape}")
        if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED:
            arimax_file_drive = os.path.join(DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED, 'features_for_arimax.csv')
            arimax_df.to_csv(arimax_file_drive)
            print(f"  ✓ Saved to Google Drive: {arimax_file_drive}")

    # Save LSTM features
    if len(lstm_features) > 0:
        lstm_df = features_df_clean[['bed_occupancy'] + lstm_features].copy()
        lstm_file_local = os.path.join(DATA_PROCESSED, 'features_for_lstm.csv')
        lstm_df.to_csv(lstm_file_local)
        print(f"  ✓ Saved to local: {lstm_file_local} | Shape: {lstm_df.shape}")
        if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED:
            lstm_file_drive = os.path.join(DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED, 'features_for_lstm.csv')
            lstm_df.to_csv(lstm_file_drive)
            print(f"  ✓ Saved to Google Drive: {lstm_file_drive}")

    # Save VAR exogenous features
    if len(var_exog_features) > 0:
        var_exog_df = features_df_clean[['bed_occupancy'] + var_exog_features].copy()
        var_exog_file_local = os.path.join(DATA_PROCESSED, 'features_for_var_exog.csv')
        var_exog_df.to_csv(var_exog_file_local)
        print(f"  ✓ Saved to local: {var_exog_file_local} | Shape: {var_exog_df.shape}")
        if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED:
            var_exog_file_drive = os.path.join(DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED, 'features_for_var_exog.csv')
            var_exog_df.to_csv(var_exog_file_drive)
            print(f"  ✓ Saved to Google Drive: {var_exog_file_drive}")

    # NEW: Save VAR multivariate endogenous features (COVID KPI + bed_occupancy)
    # Based on 02_eda.ipynb Granger causality analysis (covid_patient_pct Granger-causes bed_occupancy)
    print("\n📊 Creating VAR multivariate feature set (new KPIs)...")
    var_endogenous = ['bed_occupancy']
    # Only covid_patient_pct is Granger-causal; icu_occupancy_rate is excluded as endogenous
    var_kpi_candidates = ['covid_patient_pct']

    for kpi in var_kpi_candidates:
        if kpi in features_df_clean.columns:
            var_endogenous.append(kpi)
            print(f"  ✓ Added {kpi} to VAR endogenous variables")
        elif kpi_data is not None and kpi in kpi_data.columns:
            # Try to add from kpi_data if not in features_df_clean
            features_df_clean[kpi] = kpi_data[kpi].reindex(features_df_clean.index)
            var_endogenous.append(kpi)
            print(f"  ✓ Added {kpi} from KPI data to VAR endogenous variables")

    # Create VAR endogenous + exogenous combined file
    # FIXED: Always create the file with bed_occupancy + available features
    var_all_cols = var_endogenous + [f for f in var_exog_features if f not in var_endogenous]
    var_all_cols = [c for c in var_all_cols if c in features_df_clean.columns]

    # Ensure we have at least 2 columns for VAR (bed_occupancy + at least one other)
    if len(var_all_cols) >= 2:
        var_df = features_df_clean[var_all_cols].copy()
        var_file_local = os.path.join(DATA_PROCESSED, 'features_for_var.csv')
        var_df.to_csv(var_file_local)
        print(f"  ✓ Saved VAR features to local: {var_file_local} | Shape: {var_df.shape}")
        print(f"    Endogenous: {var_endogenous}")
        print(f"    Exogenous: {[f for f in var_all_cols if f not in var_endogenous]}")

        if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED:
            var_file_drive = os.path.join(DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED, 'features_for_var.csv')
            var_df.to_csv(var_file_drive)
            print(f"  ✓ Saved to Google Drive: {var_file_drive}")

        feature_sets['var_endogenous'] = var_endogenous
        feature_sets['var_all'] = var_all_cols
    else:
        print("  ⚠️ Insufficient features for VAR model (need at least 2)")
        print("     Available columns: {var_all_cols}")
        print("     Re-run 01b_data_preprocessing.ipynb to extract ICU/COVID KPIs")

    # Save feature sets metadata as JSON for reference
    import json
    feature_sets_file_local = os.path.join(DATA_PROCESSED, 'feature_sets_metadata.json')
    with open(feature_sets_file_local, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(feature_sets, f, indent=2)
    print(f"\n✓ Saved feature sets metadata to local: {feature_sets_file_local}")
    if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED:
        feature_sets_file_drive = os.path.join(DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED, 'feature_sets_metadata.json')
        with open(feature_sets_file_drive, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(feature_sets, f, indent=2)
        print(f"✓ Saved feature sets metadata to Google Drive: {feature_sets_file_drive}")

    # ============================================================================
    # SAVE CENTRALIZED FEATURE CONFIGURATION (for model notebooks to load)
    # ============================================================================
    # This is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for all feature definitions
    # Model notebooks (04b, 04c, 04d, 04e) should load this instead of defining their own

    feature_config_file_local = os.path.join(DATA_PROCESSED, 'feature_config.json')
    with open(feature_config_file_local, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(FEATURE_CONFIG, f, indent=2)
    print(f"✓ Saved CENTRALIZED feature config to local: {feature_config_file_local}")

    if DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED:
        feature_config_file_drive = os.path.join(DRIVE_DATA_PROCESSED, 'feature_config.json')
        with open(feature_config_file_drive, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(FEATURE_CONFIG, f, indent=2)
        print(f"✓ Saved CENTRALIZED feature config to Google Drive: {feature_config_file_drive}")

    print(f"\n📋 CENTRALIZED FEATURE CONFIG SAVED:")
    print(f"   Model notebooks should load 'feature_config.json' instead of defining features locally")
    print(f"   Config includes: critical_features, high_priority_features, kpi_features,")
    print(f"                    external_features, arimax, random_forest, lstm, var, baseline")

    print(f"\nFeature sets created for:")
    for model_type, features in feature_sets.items():
        print(f"  - {model_type}: {len(features)} features")
else:
    print("No feature-engineered data available to create feature sets")

# Optional: Visualize feature distributions and relationships
# This helps understand the features and identify potential issues
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

if len(features_df_clean) > 0 and 'bed_occupancy' in features_df_clean.columns:
    print("Creating feature visualizations...")

    # Calculate feature importance if not already calculated
    if 'feature_importance' not in locals():
        feature_importance = []
        for col in feature_cols:
            if col != 'bed_occupancy' and col in features_df_clean.columns:
                try:
                    corr = features_df_clean[col].corr(features_df_clean['bed_occupancy'])
                    if not np.isnan(corr):
                        feature_importance.append((col, abs(corr), corr))
                except:
                    pass
        feature_importance.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)

    # 1. Feature correlation heatmap (top features only)
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("📊 PLOT 1: Feature Correlation Heatmap")
    print("="*60)
    print("Purpose: Visualize pairwise correlations between top features and target variable")
    print("Interpretation:")
    print("  - Red colors = positive correlation (features increase together)")
    print("  - Blue colors = negative correlation (features move in opposite directions)")
    print("  - White/light colors = low correlation (features are independent)")
    print("  - Darker colors = stronger correlation")
    print("  - Diagonal shows self-correlation (always 1.0)")
    print("  - Look for dark red/blue squares to identify highly correlated feature pairs")
    print("    (may indicate multicollinearity if >0.9)")

    if len(feature_importance) > 0:
        top_features = [feat[0] for feat in feature_importance[:15]] + ['bed_occupancy']
        top_features = [f for f in top_features if f in features_df_clean.columns]

        if len(top_features) > 1:
            print(f"\n  Plotting correlations for top {len(top_features)-1} features + target:")
            print(f"  Features: {', '.join(top_features[:-1])}")
            print(f"  Target: {top_features[-1]}")

            plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
            corr_matrix = features_df_clean[top_features].corr()

            # Print some key correlations for context
            print(f"\n  Key correlations with target (bed_occupancy):")
            target_corrs = corr_matrix['bed_occupancy'].drop('bed_occupancy').sort_values(ascending=False)
            print(f"    Top 5 positive: {dict(target_corrs.head())}")
            if (target_corrs < 0).any():
                print(f"    Top negative: {dict(target_corrs[target_corrs < 0].head())}")

            # Show correlation values on the heatmap for easier interpretation
            sns.heatmap(
                corr_matrix,
                annot=True,
                fmt='.2f',
                cmap='coolwarm',
                center=0,
                square=True,
                linewidths=0.5,
                cbar_kws={"shrink": 0.8},
            )
            plt.title('Feature Correlation Heatmap (Top 15 Features)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
            plt.tight_layout()
            plt.show()
            print("  ✓ Plot displayed: Correlation heatmap shows relationships between top features")
        else:
            print("  ⚠️  Insufficient features to create heatmap")
    else:
        print("  ⚠️  No feature importance calculated - cannot create heatmap")

    # 2. Feature importance bar chart
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("📊 PLOT 2: Feature Importance Bar Chart")
    print("="*60)
    print("Purpose: Rank features by their correlation with the target variable (bed occupancy)")
    print("Interpretation:")
    print("  - Longer bars = stronger relationship with bed occupancy")
    print("  - Green bars = positive correlation (feature increases → bed occupancy increases)")
    print("  - Red bars = negative correlation (feature increases → bed occupancy decreases)")
    print("  - Features near top = most predictive features")
    print("  - Features near bottom = less predictive (but may still be useful)")
    print("  - Values range from -1 (perfect negative) to +1 (perfect positive)")

    if len(feature_importance) > 0:
        top_20 = feature_importance[:20]
        features_names = [feat[0] for feat in top_20]
        correlations = [feat[2] for feat in top_20]  # Use signed correlation

        print(f"\n  Plotting top {len(top_20)} features by absolute correlation:")
        print(f"  Top 5 most important:")
        for i, (name, abs_corr, corr) in enumerate(top_20[:5], 1):
            direction = "positive" if corr > 0 else "negative"
            print(f"    {i}. {name:30s} | Correlation: {corr:+.4f} ({direction})")

        plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
        colors = ['green' if c > 0 else 'red' for c in correlations]
        plt.barh(range(len(features_names)), correlations, color=colors, alpha=0.7)
        plt.yticks(range(len(features_names)), features_names)
        plt.xlabel('Correlation with Bed Occupancy', fontsize=12)
        plt.title('Top 20 Feature Importance (Correlation with Bed Occupancy)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
        plt.axvline(x=0, color='black', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)
        plt.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()

        # Statistics
        positive_count = sum(1 for c in correlations if c > 0)
        negative_count = sum(1 for c in correlations if c < 0)
        print(f"  ✓ Plot displayed: {positive_count} positive correlations, {negative_count} negative correlations")
        print(f"  Strongest correlation: {max(correlations, key=abs):+.4f}")
        print(f"  Average absolute correlation: {np.mean([abs(c) for c in correlations]):.4f}")
    else:
        print("  ⚠️  No feature importance calculated - cannot create bar chart")

    # 3. Temporal feature distributions
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("📊 PLOT 3: Temporal Feature Distributions (4 subplots)")
    print("="*60)
    print("Purpose: Show how bed occupancy varies by temporal patterns (week of year, month, quarter, year)")
    print("NOTE: Data is WEEKLY (all Sundays) - day-of-week and weekend patterns are not applicable")
    print("Interpretation:")
    print("  - Compare bar heights to see which periods have higher/lower bed occupancy")
    print("  - Look for clear seasonal patterns")
    print("  - Large differences indicate strong temporal effects")
    print("  - Small differences indicate weak temporal effects")

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 10))

    # Week of Year pattern (NOTE: Data is WEEKLY - all Sundays, so day-of-week is not applicable)
    if 'week_of_year' in features_df_clean.columns:
        woy_avg = features_df_clean.groupby('week_of_year')['bed_occupancy'].mean()
        print(f"\n  Subplot 1 (Top Left): Week of Year Pattern")
        print(f"    NOTE: Data is WEEKLY (all Sundays) - showing week-of-year pattern instead of day-of-week")
        print(f"    Number of unique weeks: {len(woy_avg)}")
        print(f"    Range: {woy_avg.min():.2f} to {woy_avg.max():.2f} ({woy_avg.max() - woy_avg.min():.2f} difference)")
        print(f"    Interpretation: Shows annual seasonality - peaks/troughs indicate seasonal patterns")

        # Plot week of year pattern (use actual week indices)
        axes[0, 0].bar(woy_avg.index, woy_avg.values, color='steelblue', alpha=0.7)
        axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Week of Year', fontsize=10)
        axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Average Bed Occupancy', fontsize=10)
        axes[0, 0].set_title('Bed Occupancy by Week of Year', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
        axes[0, 0].grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
    else:
        print("  ⚠️  week_of_year feature not available")

    # Month pattern - extract from index if not in columns
    print(f"\n  Subplot 2 (Top Right): Monthly Pattern")
    month_data = features_df_clean.copy()
    month_data['_month'] = month_data.index.month
    month_avg = month_data.groupby('_month')['bed_occupancy'].mean()
    month_names = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']
    print(f"    Average bed occupancy by month:")
    for m in month_avg.index:
        print(f"      {month_names[m-1]}: {month_avg[m]:.2f}")
    print(f"    Range: {month_avg.min():.2f} to {month_avg.max():.2f} ({month_avg.max() - month_avg.min():.2f} difference)")
    print(f"    Interpretation: Shows seasonal patterns - check for peak months")
    print(f"    NOTE: Some months may have fewer data points due to data range")

    axes[0, 1].bar(month_avg.index, month_avg.values, color='coral', alpha=0.7)
    axes[0, 1].set_xticks(month_avg.index)
    axes[0, 1].set_xticklabels([month_names[m-1] for m in month_avg.index], rotation=45)
    axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Average Bed Occupancy', fontsize=10)
    axes[0, 1].set_title('Bed Occupancy by Month', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    axes[0, 1].grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

    # Quarterly pattern (more meaningful for weekly data than weekend/weekday)
    print(f"\n  Subplot 3 (Bottom Left): Quarterly Pattern")
    quarter_data = features_df_clean.copy()
    quarter_data['_quarter'] = quarter_data.index.quarter
    quarter_avg = quarter_data.groupby('_quarter')['bed_occupancy'].mean()
    quarter_names = ['Q1 (Jan-Mar)', 'Q2 (Apr-Jun)', 'Q3 (Jul-Sep)', 'Q4 (Oct-Dec)']
    print(f"    Average bed occupancy by quarter:")
    for q in quarter_avg.index:
        print(f"      {quarter_names[q-1]}: {quarter_avg[q]:.2f}")
    print(f"    Range: {quarter_avg.min():.2f} to {quarter_avg.max():.2f} ({quarter_avg.max() - quarter_avg.min():.2f} difference)")
    print(f"    Interpretation: Shows quarterly seasonality patterns")

    axes[1, 0].bar(quarter_avg.index, quarter_avg.values, color='mediumseagreen', alpha=0.7)
    axes[1, 0].set_xticks(quarter_avg.index)
    axes[1, 0].set_xticklabels([f'Q{q}' for q in quarter_avg.index])
    axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Average Bed Occupancy', fontsize=10)
    axes[1, 0].set_title('Bed Occupancy by Quarter', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    axes[1, 0].grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

    # Year-over-year comparison (more meaningful for weekly data than holidays)
    print(f"\n  Subplot 4 (Bottom Right): Yearly Pattern")
    year_data = features_df_clean.copy()
    year_data['_year'] = year_data.index.year
    year_avg = year_data.groupby('_year')['bed_occupancy'].mean()
    year_counts = year_data.groupby('_year').size()
    print(f"    Average bed occupancy by year:")
    for y in year_avg.index:
        print(f"      {y}: {year_avg[y]:.2f} ({year_counts[y]} weeks)")
    print(f"    Range: {year_avg.min():.2f} to {year_avg.max():.2f} ({year_avg.max() - year_avg.min():.2f} difference)")
    print(f"    Interpretation: Shows year-over-year trends (COVID impact, recovery, etc.)")

    axes[1, 1].bar(year_avg.index.astype(str), year_avg.values, color='gold', alpha=0.7)
    axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Average Bed Occupancy', fontsize=10)
    axes[1, 1].set_title('Bed Occupancy by Year', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=10)
    axes[1, 1].grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("✅ ALL FEATURE VISUALIZATIONS COMPLETE")
    print("="*60)
    print("Summary:")
    print("  - Plot 1: Feature correlation heatmap (shows multicollinearity patterns)")
    print("  - Plot 2: Feature importance bar chart (ranks features by predictive power)")
    print("  - Plot 3: Temporal distributions (shows week-of-year, monthly, quarterly, yearly patterns)")
    print("\n  Use these plots to:")
    print("    • Identify highly correlated features (potential multicollinearity)")
    print("    • Understand which features are most predictive")
    print("    • Validate temporal patterns in the data")
    print("="*60)
else:

Summary¶

This notebook performs feature engineering based on EDA findings from 02_eda.ipynb:

EDA-Driven Feature Engineering:

  • ✅ Lag features based on ACF/PACF analysis: Lags 1, 3, 4, 52 (instead of arbitrary lags)
  • ✅ External features (correlation-based selection):
    • ili (r = 0.387, strongest flu predictor)
    • temp_min (r = -0.254, strongest weather predictor)
    • Excluded: flu_activity_level, wili (redundant with ili), temp_avg, temp_max (redundant with temp_min)
  • ✅ Differencing features for stationarity (ADF p=0.21, KPSS p=0.01)
  • ✅ Lagged external features for predictive modeling (ili_lag_1, temp_min_lag_1 to avoid data leakage)

Standard Feature Engineering:

  • ✅ Created temporal features (quarter, day of year, is_weekend, holidays)
  • ✅ Added cyclical encoding (sin/cos) for quarter and day of year
  • ✅ Added holiday indicators and interaction features (holiday × weekend)
  • ✅ Created rolling statistics (mean, median, std for 4, 13, 52-week windows)
  • ✅ Added change features (week-over-week)
  • ✅ Added KPI features with capacity constraints (lagged to avoid data leakage)
  • ✅ Feature validation (constant features, multicollinearity checks)
  • ✅ Feature importance analysis
  • ✅ Advanced features (percentiles, volatility, Fourier harmonics, trends)
  • ✅ Cleaned and saved feature-engineered dataset
  • ✅ Created model-specific feature sets (ARIMAX, LSTM, VAR) with external features

Key Features (EDA-Driven):

  • External features: ili, temp_min (strongest non-redundant predictors from EDA)
  • Lag features: Based on ACF/PACF analysis (lags 1, 3, 4, 52)
  • Differencing features: For ARIMA stationarity (data is non-stationary per ADF/KPSS)
  • Cyclical encoding (sin/cos): For quarter and day of year seasonality
  • Rolling statistics: 4-week, 13-week, 52-week windows for weekly data
  • Lagged external features: ili_lag_1, ili_lag_4, temp_min_lag_1 (to avoid data leakage)

EDA Insights Applied:

  • ACF lag 1: r = 0.898 (very strong autocorrelation)
  • PACF significant at lags 1, 3, 4, 10, 14
  • 52-week seasonality (moderate strength: 0.375)
  • Non-stationary: ADF p=0.21, KPSS p=0.01 → Differencing added
  • External correlations: ili (0.490), flu (0.385), temp (-0.221)

Output Files:

  • data/processed/occupancy_with_features.csv - Full dataset with all engineered features
  • data/processed/features_only.csv - Feature columns only (excludes target variable)
  • data/processed/features_for_arimax.csv - Features for ARIMAX/SARIMAX (includes external)
  • data/processed/features_for_lstm.csv - Features for LSTM (includes external + lags)
  • data/processed/features_for_var_exog.csv - Exogenous features for VAR (includes external)
  • data/processed/feature_sets_metadata.json - Feature sets metadata
  • data/processed/feature_selection_report.json - Feature selection report

Next Steps: Proceed to 04a_baseline_models.ipynb to train forecasting models with these EDA-informed features.
